circulatory.name: Anterior cerebral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The anterior cerebral artery (ACA) is one of a pair of cerebral arteries that supplies oxygenated blood to most midline portions of the frontal lobes and superior medial parietal lobes of the brain.

circulatory.name: Anterior cerebral artery (right)

circulatory.name: Anterior circumflex humeral vein (right)

circulatory.name: Anterior communicating artery
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the anterior communicating artery is a blood vessel of the brain that connects the left and right anterior cerebral arteries.

circulatory.name: Anterior division of retromandibular vein (left)
circulatory.description: The retromandibular vein emerges from the confluence of several veins, in front of the ear, and reaches the facial vein.

circulatory.name: Anterior division of retromandibular vein (right)

circulatory.name: Anterior ethmoidal artery (left)

circulatory.name: Anterior ethmoidal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The anterior ethmoidal artery, is a branch of the ophthalmic artery in the orbit.

circulatory.name: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) is one of three pairs of arteries that supplies blood to the cerebellum. It arises from the basilar artery on each side at the level of the junction between the medulla oblongata and the pons in the brainstem.

circulatory.name: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) is one of three pairs of arteries that supplies blood to the cerebellum. It arises from the basilar artery on each side at the level of the junction between the medulla oblongata and the pons in the brainstem.

circulatory.name: Anterior intercavernous sinus
circulatory.description: The intercavernous sinuses are two in number, an anterior and a posterior, and connect the two cavernous sinuses[1] across the middle line.

circulatory.name: Anterior jugular vein (left)

circulatory.name: Anterior jugular vein (right)

circulatory.name: Anterior spinal artery (right)

circulatory.name: Anterior tibial veins (right)

circulatory.description: The aortic arch, arch of the aorta, or transverse aortic arch (English:) is the part of the aorta between the ascending and descending aorta.

circulatory.name: Appendicular artery
circulatory.description: The appendicular artery, also known as appendiceal artery, commonly arises from the terminal branch of the ileocolic artery, or less commonly from the posterior cecal artery or an ileal artery.

circulatory.name: Ascending aorta
circulatory.description: The ascending aorta (AAo) is a portion of the aorta commencing at the upper part of the base of the left ventricle, on a level with the lower border of the third costal cartilage behind the left half of the sternum.

circulatory.name: Ascending pharyngeal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The ascending pharyngeal artery is an artery in the neck that supplies the pharynx, developing from the proximal part of the embryonic second aortic arch.

circulatory.name: Ascending pharyngeal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The ascending pharyngeal artery is an artery in the neck that supplies the pharynx, developing from the proximal part of the embryonic second aortic arch.

circulatory.name: Axillary artery (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the axillary artery is a large blood vessel that conveys oxygenated blood to the lateral aspect of the thorax, the axilla (armpit) and the upper limb.

circulatory.name: Axillary artery (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the axillary artery is a large blood vessel that conveys oxygenated blood to the lateral aspect of the thorax, the axilla (armpit) and the upper limb.

circulatory.name: Axillary vein (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the axillary vein is a large blood vessel that conveys blood from the lateral aspect of the thorax, axilla (armpit) and upper limb toward the heart.

circulatory.name: Axillary vein (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the axillary vein is a large blood vessel that conveys blood from the lateral aspect of the thorax, axilla (armpit) and upper limb toward the heart.

circulatory.name: Azygos vein
circulatory.description: The azygos vein is a vein running up the right side of the thoracic vertebral column draining itself towards the superior vena cava.

circulatory.name: Basilar artery
circulatory.description: The basilar artery  is one of the arteries that supplies the brain with oxygen-rich blood.

circulatory.name: Basilar venous plexus
circulatory.description: The basilar plexus (transverse or basilar sinus) consists of several interlacing venous channels between the layers of the dura mater over the basilar part of the occipital bone (the clivus), and serves to connect the two inferior petrosal sinuses.

circulatory.name: Basilic vein (left)
circulatory.description: The basilic vein is a large superficial vein of the upper limb that helps drain parts of the hand and forearm.

circulatory.name: Basilic vein (right)
circulatory.description: The basilic vein is a large superficial vein of the upper limb that helps drain parts of the hand and forearm.

circulatory.name: Bifurcation of pulmonary trunk
circulatory.description: The site of the division of the pulmonary trunk into right and left pulmonary arteries.

circulatory.name: Brachial artery (left)
circulatory.description: The brachial artery is the major blood vessel of the (upper) arm.

circulatory.name: Brachial artery (right)
circulatory.description: The brachial artery is the major blood vessel of the (upper) arm.

circulatory.name: Brachial veins (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the brachial veins are venae comitantes of the brachial artery in the arm proper.

circulatory.name: Brachial veins (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the brachial veins are venae comitantes of the brachial artery in the arm proper.

circulatory.name: Brachiocephalic trunk
circulatory.description: The brachiocephalic arterial trunk is an artery that arises from the aorta, it is located in the superior mediastinum and carries oxygenated blood to the right upper limb, the head and the neck.

circulatory.name: Buccal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The buccal artery (buccinator artery) is a small artery in the head.

circulatory.name: Buccal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The buccal artery (buccinator artery) is a small artery in the head.

circulatory.name: Callosomarginal artery (left)
circulatory.description: A2 extends from the AComm to the bifurcation forming the pericallosal and callosomarginal arteries.

circulatory.name: Callosomarginal artery (right)
circulatory.description: A2 extends from the AComm to the bifurcation forming the pericallosal and callosomarginal arteries.

circulatory.name: Cavernous sinus (left)
circulatory.description: The cavernous sinus within the human head is one of the dural venous sinuses creating a cavity called the lateral sellar compartment bordered by the temporal bone of the skull and the sphenoid bone, lateral to the sella turcica.

circulatory.name: Cavernous sinus (right)
circulatory.description: The cavernous sinus within the human head is one of the dural venous sinuses creating a cavity called the lateral sellar compartment bordered by the temporal bone of the skull and the sphenoid bone, lateral to the sella turcica.

circulatory.name: Central retinal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The central retinal artery (retinal artery) branches off the ophthalmic artery, running inferior to the optic nerve within its dural sheath to the eyeball.

circulatory.name: Central retinal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The central retinal artery (retinal artery) branches off the ophthalmic artery, running inferior to the optic nerve within its dural sheath to the eyeball.

circulatory.name: Cephalic vein (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the cephalic vein is a superficial vein in the arm.

circulatory.name: Cephalic vein (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the cephalic vein is a superficial vein in the arm.

circulatory.name: Circumflex artery of heart
circulatory.description: The "LCX", or left circumflex artery (or circumflex artery, or circumflex branch of the left coronary artery) is an artery of the heart.

circulatory.name: Circumflex scapular artery (left)
circulatory.description: The circumflex scapular artery (scapular circumflex artery, dorsalis scapulae artery) is a branch of the subscapular artery and part of the scapular anastomoses.

circulatory.name: Circumflex scapular artery (right)
circulatory.description: The circumflex scapular artery (scapular circumflex artery, dorsalis scapulae artery) is a branch of the subscapular artery and part of the scapular anastomoses.

circulatory.name: Circumflex scapular vein (left)
circulatory.description: It follows the circumflex scapular artery.

circulatory.name: Circumflex scapular vein (right)
circulatory.description: It follows the circumflex scapular artery.

circulatory.name: Coeliac trunk
circulatory.description: The coeliac  artery, also known as the coeliac trunk, or truncus coeliacus, is the first major branch of the abdominal aorta.

circulatory.name: Colic branch of ileocolic artery
circulatory.description: The colic branch of ileocolic artery is a small artery in the abdomen.

circulatory.name: Common facial vein (left)
circulatory.description: The facial vein usually unites with the anterior branch of the retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, which crosses the external carotid artery and enters the internal jugular vein at a variable point below the hyoid bone.

circulatory.name: Common facial vein (right)
circulatory.description: The facial vein usually unites with the anterior branch of the retromandibular vein to form the common facial vein, which crosses the external carotid artery and enters the internal jugular vein at a variable point below the hyoid bone.

circulatory.name: Common hepatic artery
circulatory.description: The common hepatic artery is a short blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the liver, pylorus of the stomach, duodenum, pancreas, and gallbladder.

circulatory.name: Common iliac artery (left)
circulatory.description: The common iliac artery is a large artery of the abdomen paired on each side.

circulatory.name: Common iliac artery (right)
circulatory.description: The common iliac artery is a large artery of the abdomen paired on each side.

circulatory.name: Common iliac vein (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the common iliac veins are formed by the external iliac veins and internal iliac veins.

circulatory.name: Common iliac vein (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the common iliac veins are formed by the external iliac veins and internal iliac veins.

circulatory.name: Common plantar digital arteries (left)
circulatory.description: The common plantar digital arteries are arteries of the foot.

circulatory.name: Common plantar digital arteries (right)
circulatory.description: The common plantar digital arteries are arteries of the foot.

circulatory.name: Coronary sinus
circulatory.description: The coronary sinus is a collection of veins joined together to form a large vessel that collects blood from the heart muscle (myocardium).

circulatory.name: Costocervical trunk (left)
circulatory.description: The costocervical trunk arises from the upper and back part of the second part of subclavian artery, behind the scalenus anterior on the right side, and medial to that muscle on the left side.

circulatory.name: Costocervical trunk (right)
circulatory.description: The costocervical trunk arises from the upper and back part of the second part of subclavian artery, behind the scalenus anterior on the right side, and medial to that muscle on the left side.

circulatory.name: Deep artery of penis (left)
circulatory.description: The deep artery of the penis (artery to the corpus cavernosum), one of the terminal branches of the internal pudendal, arises from that vessel while it is situated between the two fasciæ of the urogenital diaphragm (deep perineal pouch).

circulatory.name: Deep artery of penis (right)
circulatory.description: The deep artery of the penis (artery to the corpus cavernosum), one of the terminal branches of the internal pudendal, arises from that vessel while it is situated between the two fasciæ of the urogenital diaphragm (deep perineal pouch).

circulatory.name: Deep brachial artery (left)
circulatory.description: The deep artery of arm (also known as arteria profunda brachii and the deep brachial artery) is a large vessel which arises from the lateral and posterior part of the brachial artery, just below the lower border of the teres major.

circulatory.name: Deep brachial artery (right)
circulatory.description: The deep artery of arm (also known as arteria profunda brachii and the deep brachial artery) is a large vessel which arises from the lateral and posterior part of the brachial artery, just below the lower border of the teres major.

circulatory.name: Deep cervical artery (left)
circulatory.description: The deep cervical artery (Profunda cervicalis) is an artery of the neck.

circulatory.name: Deep cervical artery (right)
circulatory.description: The deep cervical artery (Profunda cervicalis) is an artery of the neck.

circulatory.name: Deep dorsal vein of penis
circulatory.description: The deep dorsal vein of the penis lies beneath the deep fascia of the penis; it receives the blood from the glans penis and corpora cavernosa penis and courses backward in the middle line between the dorsal arteries; near the root of the penis it passes between the two parts of the suspensory ligament and then through an aperture between the arcuate pubic ligament and the transverse ligament of the pelvis, and divides into two branches, which enter the vesical and prostatic plexuses.

circulatory.name: Deep external pudendal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The deep external pudendal artery (deep external pudic artery), is one of the pudendal arteries that is more deeply seated than the superficial external pudendal artery, passes medially across the pectineus and the adductor longus muscles; it is covered by the fascia lata, which it pierces at the medial side of the thigh, and is distributed, in the male, to the integument of the scrotum and perineum, in the female to the labia majora; its branches anastomose with the scrotal or labial branches of the perineal artery.

circulatory.name: Deep external pudendal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The deep external pudendal artery (deep external pudic artery), is one of the pudendal arteries that is more deeply seated than the superficial external pudendal artery, passes medially across the pectineus and the adductor longus muscles; it is covered by the fascia lata, which it pierces at the medial side of the thigh, and is distributed, in the male, to the integument of the scrotum and perineum, in the female to the labia majora; its branches anastomose with the scrotal or labial branches of the perineal artery.

circulatory.name: Deep femoral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The deep artery of the thigh, (profunda femoris artery or deep femoral artery) is a large branch of the femoral artery.

circulatory.name: Deep femoral artery (right)
circulatory.description: The deep artery of the thigh, (profunda femoris artery or deep femoral artery) is a large branch of the femoral artery.

circulatory.name: Deep femoral vein (left)
circulatory.description: The profunda femoris vein, (or deep femoral vein) is a large deep vein in the thigh.

circulatory.name: Deep femoral vein (right)
circulatory.description: The profunda femoris vein, (or deep femoral vein) is a large deep vein in the thigh.

circulatory.name: Deep palmar arch (left)
circulatory.description: The deep palmar arch (deep volar arch) is an arterial network found in the palm.

circulatory.name: Deep palmar arch (right)
circulatory.description: The deep palmar arch (deep volar arch) is an arterial network found in the palm.

circulatory.name: Deep plantar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The deep plantar artery (ramus plantaris profundus; communicating artery) descends into the sole of the foot, between the two heads of the 1st interosseous dorsalis, and unites with the termination of the lateral plantar artery, to complete the plantar arch.

circulatory.name: Deep plantar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The deep plantar artery (ramus plantaris profundus; communicating artery) descends into the sole of the foot, between the two heads of the 1st interosseous dorsalis, and unites with the termination of the lateral plantar artery, to complete the plantar arch.

circulatory.name: Deep venous palmar arch (left)
circulatory.description: The deep palmar arch is accompanied by a pair of venae comitantes which constitute the deep palmar venous arch.

circulatory.name: Deep venous palmar arch (right)
circulatory.description: The deep palmar arch is accompanied by a pair of venae comitantes which constitute the deep palmar venous arch.

circulatory.name: Descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery
circulatory.description: The descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery runs downward, behind the rectus femoris, upon the vastus lateralis, to which it gives offsets; one long branch descends in the muscle as far as the knee, and anastomoses with the superior lateral genicular artery.

circulatory.name: Descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery runs downward, behind the rectus femoris, upon the vastus lateralis, to which it gives offsets; one long branch descends in the muscle as far as the knee, and anastomoses with the superior lateral genicular artery.

circulatory.name: Descending palatine artery (left)
circulatory.description: The descending palatine artery is a branch of the third part of the maxillary artery supplying the hard and soft palate.

circulatory.name: Descending palatine artery (right)
circulatory.description: The descending palatine artery is a branch of the third part of the maxillary artery supplying the hard and soft palate.

circulatory.name: Dorsal artery of penis (left)
circulatory.description: The dorsal artery of the penis is an artery on the top surface of the penis.

circulatory.name: Dorsal artery of penis (right)
circulatory.description: The dorsal artery of the penis is an artery on the top surface of the penis.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital arteries of foot (left)
circulatory.description: The dorsal digital arteries of foot are small arteries which supply the toes.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital arteries of foot (right)
circulatory.description: The dorsal digital arteries of foot are small arteries which supply the toes.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital arteries of hand (left)
circulatory.description: Dorsal digital arteries arise from the bifurcation of dorsal metacarpal arteries.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital arteries of hand (right)
circulatory.description: Dorsal digital arteries arise from the bifurcation of dorsal metacarpal arteries.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital veins of foot (left)
circulatory.description: On the dorsum of the foot the dorsal digital veins receive, in the clefts between the toes, the intercapitular veins from the plantar venous arch and join to form short common digital veins.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital veins of foot (right)
circulatory.description: On the dorsum of the foot the dorsal digital veins receive, in the clefts between the toes, the intercapitular veins from the plantar venous arch and join to form short common digital veins.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital veins of hand (left)
circulatory.description: The dorsal venous network of the hand is a network of veins within the superficial fascia on the dorsum (backside) of hand.

circulatory.name: Dorsal digital veins of hand (right)
circulatory.description: The dorsal venous network of the hand is a network of veins within the superficial fascia on the dorsum (backside) of hand.

circulatory.name: Dorsal metacarpal arteries (left)
circulatory.description: Most of the dorsal metacarpal arteries arise from the dorsal carpal arch and run downward on the second, third, and fourth dorsal interossei of the hand and bifurcate into the dorsal digital arteries.

circulatory.name: Dorsal metacarpal arteries (right)
circulatory.description: Most of the dorsal metacarpal arteries arise from the dorsal carpal arch and run downward on the second, third, and fourth dorsal interossei of the hand and bifurcate into the dorsal digital arteries.

circulatory.name: Dorsal metatarsal arteries (left)
circulatory.description: The arcuate artery of the foot gives off the second, third, and fourth dorsal metatarsal arteries, which run forward upon the corresponding Interossei dorsales; in the clefts between the toes, each divides into two dorsal digital branches for the adjoining toes.

circulatory.name: Dorsal metatarsal arteries (right)
circulatory.description: The arcuate artery of the foot gives off the second, third, and fourth dorsal metatarsal arteries, which run forward upon the corresponding Interossei dorsales; in the clefts between the toes, each divides into two dorsal digital branches for the adjoining toes.

circulatory.name: Dorsal metatarsal veins (left)
circulatory.description: The dorsal metatarsal veins are veins which drain the metatarsus of the foot.

circulatory.name: Dorsal metatarsal veins (right)
circulatory.description: The dorsal metatarsal veins are veins which drain the metatarsus of the foot.

circulatory.name: Dorsal venous arch of foot (left)
circulatory.description: The dorsal venous arch of the foot is a superficial vein that connects the small saphenous vein and the great saphenous vein.

circulatory.name: Dorsal venous arch of foot (right)
circulatory.description: The dorsal venous arch of the foot is a superficial vein that connects the small saphenous vein and the great saphenous vein.

circulatory.name: Dorsal venous network of hand (left)
circulatory.description: The dorsal venous network of the hand is a network of veins within the superficial fascia on the dorsum (backside) of hand.

circulatory.name: Dorsal venous network of hand (right)
circulatory.description: The dorsal venous network of the hand is a network of veins within the superficial fascia on the dorsum (backside) of hand.

circulatory.name: Dorsalis pedis artery (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the dorsalis pedis artery (dorsal artery of foot) is a blood vessel of the lower limb.

circulatory.name: Dorsalis pedis artery (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the dorsalis pedis artery (dorsal artery of foot) is a blood vessel of the lower limb.

circulatory.name: External carotid artery (left)
circulatory.description: The external carotid artery is a major artery of the head and neck.

circulatory.name: External carotid artery (right)
circulatory.description: The external carotid artery is a major artery of the head and neck.

circulatory.name: External iliac artery (left)
circulatory.description: The external iliac arteries are two major arteries which bifurcate off the common iliac arteries anterior to the sacroiliac joint of the pelvis.

circulatory.name: External iliac artery (right)
circulatory.description: The external iliac arteries are two major arteries which bifurcate off the common iliac arteries anterior to the sacroiliac joint of the pelvis.

circulatory.name: External iliac vein (right)
circulatory.description: The external iliac veins are large veins that connect the femoral veins to the common iliac veins.

circulatory.name: External jugular vein (left)
circulatory.description: The external jugular vein receives the greater part of the blood from the exterior of the cranium and the deep parts of the face, being formed by the junction of the posterior division of the retromandibular vein with the posterior auricular vein.

circulatory.name: External jugular vein (right)
circulatory.description: The external jugular vein receives the greater part of the blood from the exterior of the cranium and the deep parts of the face, being formed by the junction of the posterior division of the retromandibular vein with the posterior auricular vein.

circulatory.name: External pudendal veins (left)
circulatory.description: The external pudendal veins (deep pudendal & superficial pudendal) are veins of the pelvis which drain into the great saphenous vein.

circulatory.name: External pudendal veins (right)
circulatory.description: The external pudendal veins (deep pudendal & superficial pudendal) are veins of the pelvis which drain into the great saphenous vein.

circulatory.name: Facial artery (left)
circulatory.description: The facial artery (external maxillary artery in older texts) is a branch of the external carotid artery that supplies structures of the superficial face.

circulatory.name: Facial artery (right)
circulatory.description: The facial artery (external maxillary artery in older texts) is a branch of the external carotid artery that supplies structures of the superficial face.

circulatory.name: Facial vein (right)
circulatory.description: The facial vein (or anterior facial vein) is a relatively large vein in the human face.

circulatory.name: Femoral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The femoral artery is a large artery in the thigh and the main arterial supply to the thigh and leg.

circulatory.name: Femoral artery (right)
circulatory.description: The femoral artery is a large artery in the thigh and the main arterial supply to the thigh and leg.

circulatory.name: Femoral vein (left)
circulatory.description: In the human body, the femoral vein is a blood vessel that accompanies the femoral artery in the femoral sheath.

circulatory.name: Femoral vein (right)
circulatory.description: In the human body, the femoral vein is a blood vessel that accompanies the femoral artery in the femoral sheath.

circulatory.name: Fibular artery (left)
circulatory.description: In anatomy, the fibular artery, also known as the peroneal artery, supplies blood to the lateral compartment of the leg.

circulatory.name: Fibular artery (right)
circulatory.description: In anatomy, the fibular artery, also known as the peroneal artery, supplies blood to the lateral compartment of the leg.

circulatory.description: In anatomy, the fibular veins (also known as peroneal veins) are accompanying veins (venae comitantes) of the fibular artery.

circulatory.name: Genicular veins (left)

circulatory.name: Genicular veins (right)

circulatory.name: Great cardiac vein
circulatory.description: The great cardiac vein (left coronary vein) begins at the apex of the heart and ascends along the anterior longitudinal sulcus to the base of the ventricles. It then curves around the left margin of the heart to reach the posterior surface.

circulatory.name: Great saphenous vein (left)
circulatory.description: The great saphenous vein (GSV, alternately "long saphenous vein";) is a large, subcutaneous, superficial vein of the leg.

circulatory.name: Great saphenous vein (right)
circulatory.description: The great saphenous vein (GSV, alternately "long saphenous vein";) is a large, subcutaneous, superficial vein of the leg.

circulatory.name: Greater palatine artery (left)
circulatory.description: The greater palatine artery is a branch of the descending palatine artery (a terminal branch of the maxillary artery) and contributes to the blood supply of the hard palate and nasal septum.

circulatory.name: Greater palatine artery (right)
circulatory.description: The greater palatine artery is a branch of the descending palatine artery (a terminal branch of the maxillary artery) and contributes to the blood supply of the hard palate and nasal septum.

circulatory.name: Hemi-azygos vein
circulatory.description: The hemi-azygos vein (vena azygos minor inferior) is a vein running superiorly in the lower thoracic region, just to the left side of the vertebral column.

circulatory.name: Hepatic portal vein
circulatory.description: The portal vein or hepatic portal vein (HPV) is a blood vessel that carries blood from the gastrointestinal tract, gallbladder, pancreas and spleen to the liver.

circulatory.name: Hepatic veins
circulatory.description: The hepatic veins are the veins that drain de-oxygenated blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava.

circulatory.name: Ileal branch of ileocolic artery
circulatory.description: The ileal branch of ileocolic artery is a branch of the ileocolic artery.

circulatory.name: Iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The iliac branch of the iliolumbar artery (ramus iliacus) descends to supply the iliacus muscle; some offsets, running between the muscle and the bone, anastomose with the iliac branches of the obturator artery; one of these enters an oblique canal to supply the bone, while others run along the crest of the ilium, distributing branches to the gluteal and abdominal muscles, and anastomosing in their course with the superior gluteal artery, iliac circumflex artery, and the lateral circumflex femoral artery.

circulatory.name: Iliacus branch of iliolumbar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The iliac branch of the iliolumbar artery (ramus iliacus) descends to supply the iliacus muscle; some offsets, running between the muscle and the bone, anastomose with the iliac branches of the obturator artery; one of these enters an oblique canal to supply the bone, while others run along the crest of the ilium, distributing branches to the gluteal and abdominal muscles, and anastomosing in their course with the superior gluteal artery, iliac circumflex artery, and the lateral circumflex femoral artery.

circulatory.name: Iliolumbar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The iliolumbar artery is the first branch of the posterior trunk of the internal iliac artery.

circulatory.name: Iliolumbar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The iliolumbar artery is the first branch of the posterior trunk of the internal iliac artery.

circulatory.name: Iliolumbar vein (left)
circulatory.description: The iliolumbar vein is the vena comitans of the iliolumbar artery. The obturator nerve crosses superficial to it.A single vein is found more commonly than a double vein.It drains vertebral segments four and five.It is closely related to the ascending lumbar vein.

circulatory.name: Iliolumbar vein (right)
circulatory.description: The iliolumbar vein is the vena comitans of the iliolumbar artery. The obturator nerve crosses superficial to it.A single vein is found more commonly than a double vein.It drains vertebral segments four and five.It is closely related to the ascending lumbar vein.

circulatory.name: Inferior alveolar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior alveolar artery (inferior dental artery) is an artery of the face.

circulatory.name: Inferior alveolar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior alveolar artery (inferior dental artery) is an artery of the face.

circulatory.name: Inferior epigastric artery (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, inferior epigastric artery refers to the artery that arises from the external iliac artery.

circulatory.name: Inferior epigastric artery (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, inferior epigastric artery refers to the artery that arises from the external iliac artery.

circulatory.name: Inferior epigastric vein (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, inferior epigastric vein refers to the vein that drains into the external iliac vein and anastomoses from the superior epigastric vein.

circulatory.name: Inferior epigastric vein (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, inferior epigastric vein refers to the vein that drains into the external iliac vein and anastomoses from the superior epigastric vein.

circulatory.name: Inferior gluteal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior gluteal artery (sciatic artery), the smaller of the two terminal branches of the anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery, is distributed chiefly to the buttock and back of the thigh. It passes down on the sacral plexus of nerves and the piriformis muscle, behind the internal pudendal artery.

circulatory.name: Inferior gluteal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior gluteal artery (sciatic artery), the smaller of the two terminal branches of the anterior trunk of the internal iliac artery, is distributed chiefly to the buttock and back of the thigh. It passes down on the sacral plexus of nerves and the piriformis muscle, behind the internal pudendal artery.

circulatory.name: Inferior gluteal veins (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior gluteal veins (sciatic veins), or venae comitantes of the inferior gluteal artery, begin on the upper part of the back of the thigh, where they anastomose with the medial femoral circumflex and first perforating veins.

circulatory.name: Inferior gluteal veins (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior gluteal veins (sciatic veins), or venae comitantes of the inferior gluteal artery, begin on the upper part of the back of the thigh, where they anastomose with the medial femoral circumflex and first perforating veins.

circulatory.name: Inferior labial artery (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior labial artery (inferior labial branch of facial artery) arises near the angle of the mouth as a branch of the facial artery; it passes upward and forward beneath the triangularis and, penetrating the orbicularis oris, runs in a tortuous course along the edge of the lower lip between this muscle and the mucous membrane.

circulatory.name: Inferior labial artery (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior labial artery (inferior labial branch of facial artery) arises near the angle of the mouth as a branch of the facial artery; it passes upward and forward beneath the triangularis and, penetrating the orbicularis oris, runs in a tortuous course along the edge of the lower lip between this muscle and the mucous membrane.

circulatory.name: Inferior labial veins (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior labial veins drain the blood of the inferior part of the oral region to the facial vein, then to the common facial vein, then to the internal jugular vein.

circulatory.name: Inferior labial veins (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior labial veins drain the blood of the inferior part of the oral region to the facial vein, then to the common facial vein, then to the internal jugular vein.

circulatory.name: Inferior medial genicular artery (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior medial genicular is an artery of the leg.

circulatory.name: Inferior medial genicular artery (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior medial genicular is an artery of the leg.

circulatory.name: Inferior mesenteric artery
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the inferior mesenteric artery, often abbreviated as IMA, is the third main branch of the abdominal aorta and arises at the level of L3, supplying the large intestine from the distal transverse colon to the upper part of the anal canal.

circulatory.name: Inferior mesenteric vein
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the inferior mesenteric vein (IMV) is a blood vessel that drains blood from the large intestine.

circulatory.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior ophthalmic vein is a vein of the orbit around the eye.

circulatory.name: Inferior ophthalmic vein (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior ophthalmic vein is a vein of the orbit around the eye.

circulatory.name: Inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
circulatory.description: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery (the IPDA) is a branch of the superior mesenteric artery.

circulatory.name: Inferior petrosal sinus (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior petrosal sinuses are two small sinuses situated on the inferior border of the petrous part of the temporal bone, one on each side.

circulatory.name: Inferior petrosal sinus (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior petrosal sinuses are two small sinuses situated on the inferior border of the petrous part of the temporal bone, one on each side.

circulatory.name: Inferior phrenic artery
circulatory.description: The inferior phrenic arteries are two small vessels which supply the diaphragm.

circulatory.name: Inferior sagittal sinus
circulatory.description: The inferior sagittal sinus (also known as inferior longitudinal sinus), within the human head, is an area beneath the brain which allows blood to drain outwards posteriorly from the center of the head.

circulatory.name: Inferior suprarenal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior suprarenal artery is a paired artery that supplies the adrenal gland.

circulatory.name: Inferior suprarenal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior suprarenal artery is a paired artery that supplies the adrenal gland.

circulatory.name: Inferior thyroid artery (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior thyroid artery is an artery in the neck.

circulatory.name: Inferior thyroid artery (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior thyroid artery is an artery in the neck.

circulatory.name: Inferior ulnar collateral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The inferior ulnar collateral artery (anastomotica magna artery) is an artery in the arm.

circulatory.name: Inferior ulnar collateral artery (right)
circulatory.description: The inferior ulnar collateral artery (anastomotica magna artery) is an artery in the arm.

circulatory.name: Inferior vena cava (abdominal part)
circulatory.description: The inferior vena cava is a large vein that carries the deoxygenated blood from the lower and middle body into the right atrium of the heart.

circulatory.name: Inferior vena cava (thoracic part)
circulatory.description: The inferior vena cava is a large vein that carries the deoxygenated blood from the lower and middle body into the right atrium of the heart.

circulatory.name: Infra-orbital artery (left)
circulatory.description: The infraorbital artery is an artery in the head that branches off the maxillary artery, emerging through the infraorbital foramen, just under the orbit of the eye.

circulatory.name: Infra-orbital artery (right)
circulatory.description: The infraorbital artery is an artery in the head that branches off the maxillary artery, emerging through the infraorbital foramen, just under the orbit of the eye.

circulatory.name: Intercapitular veins of foot (left)
circulatory.description: On the dorsum of the foot the dorsal digital veins receive, in the clefts between the toes, the intercapitular veins from the plantar venous arch and join to form short common digital veins.

circulatory.name: Intercapitular veins of foot (right)
circulatory.description: On the dorsum of the foot the dorsal digital veins receive, in the clefts between the toes, the intercapitular veins from the plantar venous arch and join to form short common digital veins.

circulatory.name: Internal carotid artery (left)
circulatory.description: The internal carotid artery (Latin: arteria carotis interna) is located in the inner side of the neck in contrast to the external carotid artery.

circulatory.name: Internal carotid artery (right)
circulatory.description: The internal carotid artery (Latin: arteria carotis interna) is located in the inner side of the neck in contrast to the external carotid artery.

circulatory.name: Internal iliac artery (left)
circulatory.description: The internal iliac artery (formerly known as the hypogastric artery) is the main artery of the pelvis.

circulatory.name: Internal iliac artery (right)
circulatory.description: The internal iliac artery (formerly known as the hypogastric artery) is the main artery of the pelvis.

circulatory.name: Internal iliac vein (left)
circulatory.description: The internal iliac vein (hypogastric vein) begins near the upper part of the greater sciatic foramen, passes upward behind and slightly medial to the internal iliac artery and, at the brim of the pelvis, joins with the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.

circulatory.name: Internal iliac vein (right)
circulatory.description: The internal iliac vein (hypogastric vein) begins near the upper part of the greater sciatic foramen, passes upward behind and slightly medial to the internal iliac artery and, at the brim of the pelvis, joins with the external iliac vein to form the common iliac vein.

circulatory.name: Internal jugular vein (left)
circulatory.description: The internal jugular vein is a paired jugular vein that collects blood from the brain and the superficial parts of the face and neck.

circulatory.name: Internal jugular vein (right)
circulatory.description: The internal jugular vein is a paired jugular vein that collects blood from the brain and the superficial parts of the face and neck.

circulatory.name: Internal pudendal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The internal pudendal artery is one of the three pudendal arteries that branches off the internal iliac artery.

circulatory.name: Internal pudendal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The internal pudendal artery is one of the three pudendal arteries that branches off the internal iliac artery.

circulatory.name: Internal pudendal vein (left)
circulatory.description: The internal pudendal veins (internal pudic veins) are a set of veins in the pelvis.

circulatory.name: Internal pudendal vein (right)
circulatory.description: The internal pudendal veins (internal pudic veins) are a set of veins in the pelvis.

circulatory.name: Internal thoracic artery (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the internal thoracic artery (ITA), previously commonly known as the internal mammary artery (a name still common among surgeons), is an artery that supplies the anterior chest wall and the breasts.

circulatory.name: Internal thoracic artery (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the internal thoracic artery (ITA), previously commonly known as the internal mammary artery (a name still common among surgeons), is an artery that supplies the anterior chest wall and the breasts.

circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the internal thoracic vein (previously known as the internal mammary vein) is a vessel that drains the chest wall and breasts.

circulatory.name: Internal thoracic veins (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the internal thoracic vein (previously known as the internal mammary vein) is a vessel that drains the chest wall and breasts.

circulatory.name: Lacrimal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The lacrimal artery is an artery of the orbit around the eye.

circulatory.name: Lateral circumflex femoral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The lateral circumflex femoral artery, also known as the lateral femoral circumflex artery, or the external circumflex artery, is an artery in the upper thigh.

circulatory.name: Lateral circumflex femoral artery (right)
circulatory.description: The lateral circumflex femoral artery, also known as the lateral femoral circumflex artery, or the external circumflex artery, is an artery in the upper thigh.

circulatory.description: Lateral terminal branch of the posterior cerebral artery.

circulatory.name: Lateral plantar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The lateral plantar artery (external plantar artery), much larger than the medial, passes obliquely lateralward and forward to the base of the fifth metatarsal bone.

circulatory.name: Lateral plantar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The lateral plantar artery (external plantar artery), much larger than the medial, passes obliquely lateralward and forward to the base of the fifth metatarsal bone.

circulatory.name: Lateral plantar veins (left)
circulatory.description: The lateral plantar vein lies between the flexor digitorum brevis muscle and quadratus plantae.

circulatory.name: Lateral plantar veins (right)
circulatory.description: The lateral plantar vein lies between the flexor digitorum brevis muscle and quadratus plantae.

circulatory.name: Lateral sacral veins (left)
circulatory.description: The lateral sacral veins accompany the lateral sacral arteries on the anterior surface of the sacrum and end in the hypogastric vein.

circulatory.name: Lateral sacral veins (right)
circulatory.description: The lateral sacral veins accompany the lateral sacral arteries on the anterior surface of the sacrum and end in the hypogastric vein.

circulatory.name: Lateral tarsal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The lateral tarsal artery (tarsal artery) arises from the dorsalis pedis, as that vessel crosses the navicular bone; it passes in an arched direction lateralward, lying upon the tarsal bones, and covered by extensor hallucis brevis and extensor digitorum brevis; it supplies these muscles and the articulations of the tarsus, and receives the arcuate over the base of the fifth metatarsal.

circulatory.name: Lateral tarsal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The lateral tarsal artery (tarsal artery) arises from the dorsalis pedis, as that vessel crosses the navicular bone; it passes in an arched direction lateralward, lying upon the tarsal bones, and covered by extensor hallucis brevis and extensor digitorum brevis; it supplies these muscles and the articulations of the tarsus, and receives the arcuate over the base of the fifth metatarsal.

circulatory.name: Lateral thoracic artery (left)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the lateral thoracic artery (or external mammary artery) is a blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the lateral structures of the thorax and breast.

circulatory.name: Lateral thoracic artery (right)
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the lateral thoracic artery (or external mammary artery) is a blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the lateral structures of the thorax and breast.

circulatory.name: Lateral thoracic vein (left)
circulatory.description: The lateral thoracic vein (sometimes debatably referred to as the long thoracic vein) is a tributary of the axillary vein.

circulatory.name: Lateral thoracic vein (right)
circulatory.description: The lateral thoracic vein (sometimes debatably referred to as the long thoracic vein) is a tributary of the axillary vein.

circulatory.name: Left atrium
circulatory.description: The atrium (Latin: ātrium, lit. 'entry hall') or auricle is the upper chamber through which blood enters the ventricles of the heart.

circulatory.name: Left brachiocephalic vein
circulatory.description: The left and right brachiocephalic veins (or innominate veins) are major veins in the upper chest, formed by the union of each corresponding internal jugular vein and subclavian vein.

circulatory.name: Left colic artery
circulatory.description: The left colic artery is a branch of the inferior mesenteric artery.

circulatory.name: Left common carotid artery
circulatory.description: In anatomy, the left and right common carotid arteries (carotids) (English:) are arteries that supply the head and neck with oxygenated blood; they divide in the neck to form the external and internal carotid arteries.

circulatory.name: Left coronary artery
circulatory.description: The left coronary artery (abbreviated LCA) is a coronary artery that arises from the aorta above the left cusp of the aortic valve, and feeds blood to the left side of the heart muscle.

circulatory.name: Left coronary leaflet
circulatory.description: The two leaflets of the aortic valve that are attached to the (interventricular?) septum are named the left and right leaflets, and correspond to the right and left leaflets of the aortic valve, which they face.

circulatory.name: Left gastric artery
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the left gastric artery arises from the celiac artery and runs along the superior portion of the lesser curvature of the stomach.

circulatory.name: Left gastro-omental vein
circulatory.description: The left gastroepiploic vein (left gastro-omental vein) receives branches from the antero-superior and postero-inferior surfaces of the stomach and from the greater omentum; it runs from right to left along the greater curvature of the stomach and ends in the commencement of the splenic vein.

circulatory.name: Left pulmonary artery
circulatory.description: The main pulmonary artery splits into the right and the left main pulmonary artery.

circulatory.name: Left renal artery
circulatory.description: The renal arteries are paired arteries that supply the kidneys with blood.

circulatory.name: Left renal vein
circulatory.description: There is one vein per kidney, that divides into 4 divisions upon entering the kidney:

circulatory.name: Left subclavian artery
circulatory.description: In human anatomy, the subclavian arteries are paired major arteries of the upper thorax, below the clavicle.

circulatory.name: Left subclavian vein
circulatory.description: The subclavian vein is a paired large vein, one on either side of the body, that is responsible for draining blood from the upper extremities, allowing this blood to return to the heart.

circulatory.name: Left ventricle
circulatory.description: A ventricle is one of two large chambers toward the bottom of the heart that collect and expel blood received from an atrium towards the peripheral beds within the body and lungs.

circulatory.name: Long posterior ciliary arteries (left)
circulatory.description: The long posterior ciliary arteries are arteries of the head arising, together with the other ciliary arteries, from the ophthalmic artery.

circulatory.name: Long posterior ciliary arteries (right)
circulatory.description: The long posterior ciliary arteries are arteries of the head arising, together with the other ciliary arteries, from the ophthalmic artery.

circulatory.name: Lumbar arteries (left)
circulatory.description: The lumbar arteries are arteries located in the lower back or lumbar region.

circulatory.name: Lumbar arteries (right)
circulatory.description: The lumbar arteries are arteries located in the lower back or lumbar region.

circulatory.name: Lumbar branch of iliolumbar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery (ramus lumbalis) supplies the psoas major and quadratus lumborum, anastomoses with the last lumbar artery, and sends a small spinal branch through the intervertebral foramen between the last lumbar vertebra and the sacrum, into the vertebral canal to supply the cauda equina.

circulatory.name: Lumbar branch of iliolumbar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The lumbar branch of the iliolumbar artery (ramus lumbalis) supplies the psoas major and quadratus lumborum, anastomoses with the last lumbar artery, and sends a small spinal branch through the intervertebral foramen between the last lumbar vertebra and the sacrum, into the vertebral canal to supply the cauda equina.

circulatory.name: Lumbar veins (right)

circulatory.description: The maxillary vein, or internal maxillary vein, is a vein of the head.

It is at first situated above the abductor hallucis, and then between it and the flexor digitorum brevis, both of which it supplies.

circulatory.name: Middle cardiac vein
circulatory.description: The middle cardiac vein commences at the apex of the heart; ascends in the posterior longitudinal sulcus, and ends in the coronary sinus near its right extremity.

circulatory.description: The middle colic vein drains the transverse colon.

circulatory.name: Middle collateral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The medial collateral artery (also known as the middle collateral artery) is a branch of profunda brachii artery that descends in the middle head of the triceps brachii and assists in forming the anastomosis with the interosseous recurrent artery above the olecranon of the ulna near the elbow.

circulatory.name: Plantar digital veins (right)

circulatory.name: Plantar metatarsal veins (right)

circulatory.name: Plantar venous arch (right)

circulatory.description: The subclavian vein is a paired large vein, one on either side of the body, that is responsible for draining blood from the upper extremities, allowing this blood to return to the heart.
