circulatory.name: Supratrochlear artery (left)
circulatory.description: The supratrochlear artery (or frontal artery) is one of the terminal branches of the ophthalmic artery.

circulatory.name: Supratrochlear artery (right)
circulatory.description: The supratrochlear artery (or frontal artery) is one of the terminal branches of the ophthalmic artery.

circulatory.name: Thoracic aorta
circulatory.description: The (descending) thoracic aorta is a part of the aorta located in the thorax.

circulatory.name: Thoraco-acromial artery (left)
circulatory.description: It starts at the superior border of pectoralis minor muscle and sends its branches in all the directions.

circulatory.name: Thoraco-acromial artery (right)
circulatory.description: It starts at the superior border of pectoralis minor muscle and sends its branches in all the directions.

circulatory.name: Thoracodorsal artery (left)
circulatory.description: The thoracodorsal artery is a branch of the subscapular artery.

circulatory.name: Thoracodorsal artery (right)
circulatory.description: The thoracodorsal artery is a branch of the subscapular artery.

circulatory.name: Thoracodorsal vein (left)
circulatory.description: It follows the thoraco-dorsal artery.

circulatory.name: Thoracodorsal vein (right)
circulatory.description: It follows the thoraco-dorsal artery.

circulatory.name: Thyrocervical trunk (left)
circulatory.description: The thyrocervical trunk is an artery of the neck.

circulatory.name: Thyrocervical trunk (right)
circulatory.description: The thyrocervical trunk is an artery of the neck.

circulatory.name: Transverse cervical artery (left)
circulatory.description: The transverse cervical artery (transverse artery of neck or transversa colli artery) is an artery in the neck and a branch of the thyrocervical trunk, running at a higher level than the suprascapular artery.

circulatory.name: Transverse cervical artery (right)
circulatory.description: The transverse cervical artery (transverse artery of neck or transversa colli artery) is an artery in the neck and a branch of the thyrocervical trunk, running at a higher level than the suprascapular artery.

circulatory.name: Transverse facial artery (left)
circulatory.description: The transverse facial artery is an artery that branches from the superficial temporal artery and runs across the face.

circulatory.name: Transverse facial artery (right)
circulatory.description: The transverse facial artery is an artery that branches from the superficial temporal artery and runs across the face.

circulatory.name: Transverse sinus (left)
circulatory.description: The transverse sinuses (left and right lateral sinuses), within the human head, are two areas beneath the brain which allow blood to drain from the back of the head.

circulatory.name: Transverse sinus (right)
circulatory.description: The transverse sinuses (left and right lateral sinuses), within the human head, are two areas beneath the brain which allow blood to drain from the back of the head.

circulatory.name: Ulnar artery (left)
circulatory.description: The ulnar artery is the main blood vessel, with oxygenated blood, of the medial aspects of the forearm.

circulatory.name: Ulnar artery (right)
circulatory.description: The ulnar artery is the main blood vessel, with oxygenated blood, of the medial aspects of the forearm.

circulatory.name: Ulnar veins (left)
circulatory.description: In anatomy, the ulnar veins are venae comitantes for the ulnar artery.

circulatory.name: Ulnar veins (right)
circulatory.description: In anatomy, the ulnar veins are venae comitantes for the ulnar artery.

circulatory.name: Vertebral artery (left)
circulatory.description: The vertebral arteries are major arteries of the neck.

circulatory.name: Vertebral artery (right)
circulatory.description: The vertebral arteries are major arteries of the neck.

circulatory.name: Vertebral vein (left)
circulatory.description: The vertebral vein is formed in the suboccipital triangle, from numerous small tributaries which spring from the internal vertebral venous plexuses and issue from the vertebral canal above the posterior arch of the atlas.

circulatory.name: Vertebral vein (right)
circulatory.description: The vertebral vein is formed in the suboccipital triangle, from numerous small tributaries which spring from the internal vertebral venous plexuses and issue from the vertebral canal above the posterior arch of the atlas.

digestive.name: Accessory pancreatic duct
digestive.description: Most people have just one pancreatic duct.

digestive.name: Anterior lateral segment of liver (VI)
digestive.description: It is located beneath the posterior lateral division of liver (VII), with which it forms the right lateral division of liver.

digestive.name: Anterior medial segment of liver (V)
digestive.description: It is located beneath the posterior medial segment of liver (VIII), with which it forms the right medial division of liver.

digestive.name: Ascending colon
digestive.description: The large intestine, also known as the large bowel, is the last part of the gastrointestinal tract and of the digestive system in vertebrates.

digestive.name: Bile duct
digestive.description: A bile duct is any of a number of long tube-like structures that carry bile, and is present in most vertebrates. Bile is required for the digestion of food and is secreted by the liver into passages that carry bile toward the hepatic duct.

digestive.name: Descending colon
digestive.description: The large intestine, also known as the large bowel, is the last part of the gastrointestinal tract and of the digestive system in vertebrates.

digestive.name: Duodenum
digestive.description: The duodenum is the first section of the small intestine in most higher vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles, and birds.

digestive.name: Free taenia
digestive.description: The taeniae coli (also teniae coli or tenia coli) are three separate longitudinal ribbons (taeniae meaning ribbon in Latin) of smooth muscle on the outside of the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colons.

digestive.name: Gallbladder
digestive.description: In vertebrates, the gallbladder, also known as the cholecyst, is a small hollow organ where bile is stored and concentrated before it is released into the small intestine.

digestive.name: Gingiva
digestive.description: The gums or gingiva (plural: gingivae) consist of the mucosal tissue that lies over the mandible and maxilla inside the mouth.

digestive.name: Jejunum
digestive.description: The jejunum is the second part of the small intestine in humans and most higher vertebrates, including mammals, reptiles, and birds.

digestive.name: Laryngopharynx
digestive.description: The laryngopharynx, (Latin: pars laryngea pharyngis), also known as hypopharynx, is the caudal part of the pharynx; it is the part of the throat that connects to the esophagus.

digestive.name: Left anterior lateral segment of liver (III)
digestive.description: Inferior lateral segment of the left lateral division of liver.

digestive.name: Left posterior lateral segment of liver (II)
digestive.description: Superior lateral segment of the left lateral division of liver.

digestive.name: Lesser omentum
digestive.description: The lesser omentum (small omentum or gastrohepatic omentum) is the double layer of peritoneum that extends from the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach, and to the first part of the duodenum.

digestive.name: Liver
digestive.description: The liver is an organ of the digestive system only found in vertebrates which detoxifies various metabolites, synthesizes proteins and produces biochemicals necessary for digestion and growth.

digestive.name: Meso-appendix
digestive.description: The mesentery becomes attached to the colon at the gastrointestinal margin and continues as the several regions of the mesocolon.

digestive.name: Mesocolic taenia
digestive.description: The taeniae coli (also teniae coli or tenia coli) are three separate longitudinal ribbons (taeniae meaning ribbon in Latin) of smooth muscle on the outside of the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colons.

digestive.name: Mesocolon
digestive.description: Peritoneal fold in which the vessels and nerves travel, for the suspension and the supply of the colon.

digestive.name: Nasopharynx
digestive.description: The upper portion of the pharynx, the nasopharynx, extends from the base of the skull to the upper surface of the soft palate.

digestive.name: Oesophagus
digestive.description: The oesophagus (British English; both) or esophagus (American English), informally known as the food pipe or gullet, is an organ in vertebrates through which food passes, aided by peristaltic contractions, from the pharynx to the stomach.

digestive.name: Omental taenia
digestive.description: The taeniae coli (also teniae coli or tenia coli) are three separate longitudinal ribbons (taeniae meaning ribbon in Latin) of smooth muscle on the outside of the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colons.

digestive.name: Oropharynx
digestive.description: The oropharynx lies behind the oral cavity, extending from the uvula to the level of the hyoid bone.

digestive.name: Pancreas
digestive.description: The pancreas is an organ of the digestive system and endocrine system of vertebrates.

digestive.name: Pancreatic duct
digestive.description: The pancreatic duct, or duct of Wirsung (also, the major pancreatic duct due to the existence of an accessory pancreatic duct), is a duct joining the pancreas to the common bile duct.

digestive.name: Parotid duct (left)
digestive.description: The parotid duct, or Stensen duct,is a salivary duct.

digestive.name: Parotid duct (right)
digestive.description: The parotid duct, or Stensen duct,is a salivary duct.

digestive.name: Parotid gland (left)
digestive.description: The parotid gland is a major salivary gland in many animals.

digestive.name: Parotid gland (right)
digestive.description: The parotid gland is a major salivary gland in many animals.

digestive.name: Posterior lateral segment of liver (VII)
digestive.description: It is located above the anterior lateral segment of liver (VI), with which it forms the right lateral division of liver.

digestive.name: Posterior medial segment of liver (VIII)
digestive.description: It is located above the anterior medial segment of liver (V) with which it forms the right medial division of liver.

digestive.name: Posterior segment of liver (I)
digestive.description: Segment I is the caudate lobe and is situated posterior.

digestive.name: Sigmoid colon
digestive.description: The sigmoid colon (or pelvic colon) is the part of the large intestine that is closest to the rectum and anus.

digestive.name: Soft palate
digestive.description: The soft palate (also known as the velum, palatal velum, or muscular palate) is, in mammals, the soft tissue constituting the back of the roof of the mouth.

digestive.name: Stomach
digestive.description: The stomach is a muscular, hollow organ in the gastrointestinal tract of humans and many other animals, including several invertebrates.

digestive.name: Sublingual gland (left)
digestive.description: The paired sublingual glands are major salivary glands in the mouth.

digestive.name: Sublingual gland (right)
digestive.description: The paired sublingual glands are major salivary glands in the mouth.

digestive.name: Submandibular duct (left)
digestive.description: The submandibular duct or Wharton duct or submaxillary duct, is one of the salivary excretory ducts.

digestive.name: Submandibular duct (right)
digestive.description: The submandibular duct or Wharton duct or submaxillary duct, is one of the salivary excretory ducts.

digestive.name: Submandibular gland (left)
digestive.description: The paired submandibular glands (historically known as submaxillary glands) are major salivary glands located beneath the floor of the mouth.

digestive.name: Submandibular gland (right)
digestive.description: The paired submandibular glands (historically known as submaxillary glands) are major salivary glands located beneath the floor of the mouth.

digestive.name: Tongue
digestive.description: The tongue is a muscular organ in the mouth of a typical tetrapod.

digestive.name: Transverse colon
digestive.description: The large intestine, also known as the large bowel, is the last part of the gastrointestinal tract and of the digestive system in vertebrates.

digestive.name: Uvula of palate
digestive.description: The palatine uvula, usually referred to as simply the uvula, is a conic projection from the back edge of the middle of the soft palate, composed of connective tissue containing a number of racemose glands, and some muscular fibers.

digestive.name: Vermiform appendix
digestive.description: The appendix (or vermiform appendix; also cecal [or caecal] appendix; vermix; or vermiform process) is a finger-like, blind-ended tube connected to the cecum, from which it develops in the embryo.

endocrine.name: Adenohypophysis
endocrine.description: A major organ of the endocrine system, the anterior pituitary (also called the adenohypophysis or pars anterior) is the glandular, anterior lobe that together with the posterior lobe (posterior pituitary, or the neurohypophysis) makes up the pituitary gland (hypophysis).

endocrine.name: Inferior parathyroid gland (left)
endocrine.description: The two parathyroid glands on each side which are positioned higher are called the superior parathyroid glands, while the lower two are called the inferior parathyroid glands.

endocrine.name: Inferior parathyroid gland (right)
endocrine.description: The two parathyroid glands on each side which are positioned higher are called the superior parathyroid glands, while the lower two are called the inferior parathyroid glands.

endocrine.name: Neurohypophysis
endocrine.description: The posterior pituitary (or neurohypophysis) is the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland which is part of the endocrine system.

endocrine.name: Pineal gland
endocrine.description: The pineal gland, conarium, or epiphysis cerebri, is a small endocrine gland in the brain of most vertebrates.

endocrine.name: Suprarenal gland (left)
endocrine.description: The suprarenal glands (also known as adrenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including suprarenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.

endocrine.name: Suprarenal gland (right)
endocrine.description: The suprarenal glands (also known as adrenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including suprarenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.

endocrine.name: Thyroid gland
endocrine.description: The thyroid, or thyroid gland, is an endocrine gland in vertebrates.

lymphatic.name: Anterior axillary nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: An anterior or pectoral group consists of four or five glands along the lower border of the Pectoralis minor, in relation with the lateral thoracic artery.

lymphatic.name: Anterior axillary nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: An anterior or pectoral group consists of four or five glands along the lower border of the Pectoralis minor, in relation with the lateral thoracic artery.

lymphatic.name: Apical axillary nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: An apical (or medial or subclavicular) group of six to twelve glands is situated partly posterior to the upper portion of the Pectoralis minor and partly above the upper border of this muscle.

lymphatic.name: Apical axillary nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: An apical (or medial or subclavicular) group of six to twelve glands is situated partly posterior to the upper portion of the Pectoralis minor and partly above the upper border of this muscle.

lymphatic.name: Appendicular nodes
lymphatic.description: The appendicular nodes are located along the appendicular artery.

lymphatic.name: Brachiocephalic nodes
lymphatic.description: In front of the aortic arch and of its branches; along the brachiocephalic veins.

lymphatic.name: Bucinator node (left)
lymphatic.description: The bucinator lymph node or nodes are one or more lymph nodes placed on the Buccinator opposite the angle of the mouth.

lymphatic.name: Bucinator node (right)
lymphatic.description: The bucinator lymph node or nodes are one or more lymph nodes placed on the Buccinator opposite the angle of the mouth.

lymphatic.name: Central axillary nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: A central or intermediate group of three or four large glands is imbedded in the adipose tissue near the base of the axilla.

lymphatic.name: Central axillary nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: A central or intermediate group of three or four large glands is imbedded in the adipose tissue near the base of the axilla.

lymphatic.name: Central superior mesenteric nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the superior mesenteric nodes located at the trunk of the superior mesenteric artery.

lymphatic.name: Coeliac nodes
lymphatic.description: The coeliac nodes are located around the coeliac trunk and are the second filtration relay of the stomach, the duodenum, the liver, the gallbladder, the pancreas and the spleen. They efferent vessels form a part of the intestinal trunk, the others go directly to the chyle cistern.

lymphatic.name: Cubital nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: One or two lymph nodes along the brachial artery inside the cubital fossa.

lymphatic.name: Cubital nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: One or two lymph nodes along the brachial artery inside the cubital fossa.

lymphatic.name: Cystic node
lymphatic.description: Big lympatic node next to the gallbladder.

lymphatic.name: Ileocolic nodes
lymphatic.description: The ileocolic nodes are located along the ileocolic artery.

lymphatic.name: Inferior diaphragmatic nodes
lymphatic.description: On the inferior surface of diaphragm, near the aortic hiatus.

lymphatic.name: Inferior epigastric nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: Three or four lymph nodes along the inferior epigastric artery for its territory.

lymphatic.name: Inferior epigastric nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: Three or four lymph nodes along the inferior epigastric artery for its territory.

lymphatic.name: Inferior gluteal nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: They are located along the inferior gluteal nodes for the prostate and the proximal part of the ureter.

lymphatic.name: Inferior gluteal nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: They are located along the inferior gluteal nodes for the prostate and the proximal part of the ureter.

lymphatic.name: Inferior pancreatic nodes
lymphatic.description: On the inferior border of pancreas.

lymphatic.name: Infraclavicular nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: One or two deltopectoral lymph nodes (or infraclavicular nodes) are found beside the cephalic vein, between the pectoralis major and deltoideus, immediately below the clavicle.

lymphatic.name: Infraclavicular nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: One or two deltopectoral lymph nodes (or infraclavicular nodes) are found beside the cephalic vein, between the pectoralis major and deltoideus, immediately below the clavicle.

lymphatic.name: Intercostal nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The intercostal lymph nodes (intercostal glands) occupy the posterior parts of the intercostal spaces, in relation to the intercostal vessels.

lymphatic.name: Intercostal nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The intercostal lymph nodes (intercostal glands) occupy the posterior parts of the intercostal spaces, in relation to the intercostal vessels.

lymphatic.name: Intermediate common iliac nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the common iliac nodes located behind the vascular axis, between the medial common iliac nodes and the lateral common iliac nodes.

lymphatic.name: Intermediate external iliac nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: Group of external iliac nodes located behind the vascular axis, between the medial external iliac nodes and the lateral external iliac nodes.

lymphatic.name: Intermediate external iliac nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: Group of external iliac nodes located behind the vascular axis, between the medial external iliac nodes and the lateral external iliac nodes.

lymphatic.name: Intermediate lumbar nodes
lymphatic.description: Between the aorta and the inferior vena cava.

lymphatic.name: Interpectoral nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The small interpectoral lymph nodes are located between the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles.

lymphatic.name: Interpectoral nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The small interpectoral lymph nodes are located between the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles.

lymphatic.name: Intrapulmonary nodes
lymphatic.description: The Intrapulmonary nodes or Lymphatic Vessels of the Lungs originate in two plexuses, a superficial and a deep.

lymphatic.name: Jugulodigastric node (left)
lymphatic.description: The jugulodigastric lymph nodes are large lymph nodes of the neck.

lymphatic.name: Jugulodigastric node (right)
lymphatic.description: The jugulodigastric lymph nodes are large lymph nodes of the neck.

lymphatic.name: Juxta-intestinal mesenteric nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the superior mesenteric nodes located very close to the small intestine.

lymphatic.name: Juxta-oesophageal nodes
lymphatic.description: They are located next to the oesophagus but belong to the lungs.

lymphatic.name: Lateral aortic nodes
lymphatic.description: They are located on the left side of the abdominal aorta.

lymphatic.name: Lateral axillary nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: A brachial lymph nodes (or lateral group) are group of four to six lymph nodes which lies in relation to the medial and posterior aspects of the axillary vein; the afferents of these glands drain the whole arm with the exception of that portion whose vessels accompany the cephalic vein.

lymphatic.name: Lateral axillary nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: A brachial lymph nodes (or lateral group) are group of four to six lymph nodes which lies in relation to the medial and posterior aspects of the axillary vein; the afferents of these glands drain the whole arm with the exception of that portion whose vessels accompany the cephalic vein.

lymphatic.name: Lateral caval nodes
lymphatic.description: The lateral caval nodes are located on the right of the inferior vena cava.

lymphatic.name: Lateral common iliac nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the common iliac nodes located on the lateral side of the vascular axis.

lymphatic.name: Lateral sacral nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: They are located against the sacrum; for the prostate and the neck of uterus.

lymphatic.name: Lateral sacral nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: They are located against the sacrum; for the prostate and the neck of uterus.

lymphatic.name: Left colic nodes
lymphatic.description: The left colic nodes follow the path of the left colic artery.

lymphatic.name: Mandibular node (left)
lymphatic.description: the mandibular node is located on the external side of the mandible.

lymphatic.name: Mandibular node (right)
lymphatic.description: the mandibular node is located on the external side of the mandible.

lymphatic.name: Mastoid nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The mastoid lymph nodes (retroauricular lymph nodes or posterior auricular glands) are a small group of lymph nodes, usually two in number, located just beneath the ear, on the mastoid insertion of the sternocleidomastoideus muscle, beneath the posterior auricular muscle.

lymphatic.name: Mastoid nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The mastoid lymph nodes (retroauricular lymph nodes or posterior auricular glands) are a small group of lymph nodes, usually two in number, located just beneath the ear, on the mastoid insertion of the sternocleidomastoideus muscle, beneath the posterior auricular muscle.

lymphatic.name: Medial common iliac nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the common iliac nodes located on the medial side of the vascular axis.

lymphatic.name: Middle colic nodes
lymphatic.description: The left colic nodes follow the path of the left colic artery.

lymphatic.name: Nasolabial node (left)
lymphatic.description: The nasolabial lymph node is a facial node found near the nose and upper lip.

lymphatic.name: Nasolabial node (right)
lymphatic.description: The nasolabial lymph node is a facial node found near the nose and upper lip.

lymphatic.name: Obturator nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: Located along the obturator artery.

lymphatic.name: Obturator nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: Located along the obturator artery.

lymphatic.name: Occipital nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The occipital lymph nodes, one to three in number, are located on the back of the head close to the margin of the trapezius and resting on the insertion of the semispinalis capitis.

lymphatic.name: Occipital nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The occipital lymph nodes, one to three in number, are located on the back of the head close to the margin of the trapezius and resting on the insertion of the semispinalis capitis.

lymphatic.name: Palatine tonsil (left)
lymphatic.description: Palatine tonsils, commonly called the tonsils and occasionally called the faucial tonsils, are tonsils located on the left and right sides at the back of the throat, which can often be seen as flesh-colored, pinkish lumps.

lymphatic.name: Palatine tonsil (right)
lymphatic.description: Palatine tonsils, commonly called the tonsils and occasionally called the faucial tonsils, are tonsils located on the left and right sides at the back of the throat, which can often be seen as flesh-colored, pinkish lumps.

lymphatic.name: Paracolic superior mesenteric nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the superior mesenteric nodes located next to the colon.

lymphatic.name: Parasternal nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The parasternal lymph nodes (or sternal glands) are placed at the anterior ends of the intercostal spaces, by the side of the internal thoracic artery.

lymphatic.name: Parasternal nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The parasternal lymph nodes (or sternal glands) are placed at the anterior ends of the intercostal spaces, by the side of the internal thoracic artery.

lymphatic.name: Paratracheal cervical nodes
lymphatic.description: The right and left paratracheal nodes (or paratracheal chains) are groups of lymph nodes located laterally to the trachea; unlike the pretracheal nodes that are located in front of it.

lymphatic.name: Posterior axillary nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: A posterior or subscapular group of six or seven glands is placed along the lower margin of the posterior wall of the axilla in the course of the subscapular artery.

lymphatic.name: Posterior axillary nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: A posterior or subscapular group of six or seven glands is placed along the lower margin of the posterior wall of the axilla in the course of the subscapular artery.

lymphatic.name: Postvesical nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the paravesical nodes located behind the urinary bladder.

lymphatic.name: Pre-aortic nodes
lymphatic.description: The preaortic lymph nodes lie in front of the aorta, and may be divided into celiac lymph nodes, superior mesenteric lymph nodes, and inferior mesenteric lymph nodes groups, arranged around the origins of the corresponding arteries.

lymphatic.name: Precaecal nodes
lymphatic.description: The precaecal nodes are located along the anterior caecal artery.

lymphatic.name: Precaval nodes
lymphatic.description: They are located in front of the inferior vena cava.

lymphatic.name: Prepericardial nodes
lymphatic.description: Located between the sternum and the pericardium, the prepericardial nodes drain the sternum and the anterior part of the pericardium.

lymphatic.name: Pretracheal nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The pretracheal lymph nodes are lymph nodes located anterior to the trachea in the neck.

lymphatic.name: Pretracheal nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The pretracheal lymph nodes are lymph nodes located anterior to the trachea in the neck.

lymphatic.name: Prevertebral nodes
lymphatic.description: The prevertebral lymph nodes are located between the oesophagus and the vertebral column.

lymphatic.name: Prevesical nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the vesical nodes located between the urinary bladder and the pubic symphysis.

lymphatic.name: Retro-aortic nodes
lymphatic.description: The retroaortic lymph nodes (or postaortic lymph nodes) are placed below the cisterna chyli, on the bodies of the third and fourth lumbar vertebrae.

lymphatic.name: Retrocaecal nodes
lymphatic.description: The retrocaecal are located along the posterior caecal artery.

lymphatic.name: Retrocaval nodes
lymphatic.description: The retrocaval nodes are located behind the inferior vena cava.

lymphatic.name: Retropharyngeal nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The retropharyngeal lymph nodes, from one to three in number, lie in the buccopharyngeal fascia, behind the upper part of the pharynx and in front of the arch of the atlas, being separated, however, from the latter by the Longus capitis.

lymphatic.name: Retropharyngeal nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The retropharyngeal lymph nodes, from one to three in number, lie in the buccopharyngeal fascia, behind the upper part of the pharynx and in front of the arch of the atlas, being separated, however, from the latter by the Longus capitis.

lymphatic.name: Right colic nodes
lymphatic.description: The left colic nodes follow the path of the left colic artery.

lymphatic.name: Right gastric nodes
lymphatic.description: On the lesser curvature of stomach, they follow the path of the left/right gastric arteries.

lymphatic.name: Right gastro-omental nodes
lymphatic.description: The right and left gastro-omental nodes are located on the great curvature of stomach on the path of the left/right gastro-omental arteries.

lymphatic.name: Sigmoid nodes
lymphatic.description: Located along the sigmoid artery, for the sigmoid colon and the contiguous colic segment.

lymphatic.name: Spleen
lymphatic.description: The spleen is an organ found in all vertebrates.

lymphatic.name: Splenic nodes
lymphatic.description: The splenic lymph nodes are found at the splenic hilum and in relation to the tail of the pancreas (pancreaticolienal lymph nodes).

lymphatic.name: Subaortic nodes
lymphatic.description: Those of the common iliac nodes located beneath the aortic bifurcation, in front of the 4th lumbar vertebra (Vertebra T4).

lymphatic.name: Submandibular nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The submandibular lymph nodes (submaxillary glands in older texts), three to six in number, are lymph nodes beneath the body of the mandible in the submandibular triangle, and rest on the superficial surface of the submandibular gland.

lymphatic.name: Submandibular nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The submandibular lymph nodes (submaxillary glands in older texts), three to six in number, are lymph nodes beneath the body of the mandible in the submandibular triangle, and rest on the superficial surface of the submandibular gland.

lymphatic.name: Submental nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The submental glands (or suprahyoid) are situated between the anterior bellies of the digastric muscle and the hyoid bone.

lymphatic.name: Submental nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The submental glands (or suprahyoid) are situated between the anterior bellies of the digastric muscle and the hyoid bone.

lymphatic.name: Superficial popliteal nodes (left)
lymphatic.description: The superficial popliteal nodes are located at the proximal extremity of the lesser saphenous vein and drain the lymph of the lateral border of the foot and of the leg.

lymphatic.name: Superficial popliteal nodes (right)
lymphatic.description: The superficial popliteal nodes are located at the proximal extremity of the lesser saphenous vein and drain the lymph of the lateral border of the foot and of the leg.

muscular.name: Superior tarsus (right)

muscular.name: Supraspinatus muscle (left)

muscular.name: Supraspinatus muscle (right)

muscular.name: Thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-arytenoid muscle (left)

muscular.name: Thyro-epiglottic part of thyro-arytenoid muscle (right)

muscular.name: Tibialis anterior muscle (left)
muscular.description: The tibialis anterior muscle is a muscle in humans that originates along the upper two-thirds of the lateral (outside) surface of the tibia and inserts into the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal bones of the foot.

muscular.name: Tibialis anterior muscle (right)

muscular.name: Tibialis posterior muscle (left)

muscular.name: Tibialis posterior muscle (right)

muscular.name: Transverse arytenoid muscle
muscular.description: The arytenoid muscle /ærɪˈtiːnɔɪd/ is a single muscle of the larynx.

muscular.name: Transverse head of adductor hallucis (left)
muscular.description: The transverse head (Transversus pedis) is a narrow, flat fasciculus which arises from the plantar metatarsophalangeal ligaments of the third, fourth, and fifth toes (sometimes only from the third and fourth), and from the transverse ligament of the metatarsals.

muscular.name: Transverse head of adductor hallucis (right)

muscular.name: Transverse head of adductor pollicis (left)
muscular.description: In human anatomy, the adductor pollicis muscle is a muscle in the hand that functions to adduct the thumb.

muscular.name: Transverse head of adductor pollicis (right)
muscular.description: In human anatomy, the adductor pollicis muscle is a muscle in the hand that functions to adduct the thumb.

muscular.name: Transverse part of trapezius muscle (left)
muscular.description: The trapezius is a large paired trapezoid-shaped surface muscle that extends longitudinally from the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae of the spine and laterally to the spine of the scapula.

muscular.name: Transverse part of trapezius muscle (right)
muscular.description: The trapezius is a large paired trapezoid-shaped surface muscle that extends longitudinally from the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae of the spine and laterally to the spine of the scapula.

muscular.name: Transversus abdominis muscle (left)
muscular.description: The transverse abdominal muscle (TVA), also known as the transverse abdominis, transversalis muscle and transversus abdominis muscle, is a muscle layer of the anterior and lateral (front and side) abdominal wall which is deep to (layered below) the internal oblique muscle.

muscular.name: Transversus abdominis muscle (right)

muscular.name: Transversus thoracis muscle (left)
muscular.description: The transversus thoracis muscle, also known as triangularis sterni, lies internal to the thoracic cage, anteriorly.

muscular.name: Transversus thoracis muscle (right)
muscular.description: The transversus thoracis muscle, also known as triangularis sterni, lies internal to the thoracic cage, anteriorly.

muscular.name: Trochlea of superior oblique muscle (left)

muscular.name: Trochlea of superior oblique muscle (right)

muscular.name: Zygomaticus major muscle (left)
muscular.description: The zygomaticus major muscle is a muscle of the human body. It extends from each zygomatic arch (cheekbone) to the corners of the mouth.

muscular.name: Zygomaticus major muscle (right)
muscular.description: The zygomaticus major muscle is a muscle of the human body. It extends from each zygomatic arch (cheekbone) to the corners of the mouth.

muscular.name: Zygomaticus minor muscle (left)
muscular.description: The zygomaticus minor muscle is a muscle of facial expression. It originates from the zygomatic bone, lateral to the rest of the levator labii superioris muscle, and inserts into the outer part of the upper lip.

muscular.name: Zygomaticus minor muscle (right)

nervous.name: Abducens nerve (VI) (left)
nervous.description: The abducens nerve (or abducent nerve) is the sixth cranial nerve (CNVI), in humans, that controls the movement of the lateral rectus muscle, responsible for outward gaze.

nervous.name: Abducens nerve (VI) (right)
nervous.description: The abducens nerve (or abducent nerve) is the sixth cranial nerve (CNVI), in humans, that controls the movement of the lateral rectus muscle, responsible for outward gaze.

nervous.name: Accessory nerve (XI) (left)
nervous.description: The accessory nerve is a cranial nerve that supplies the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.

nervous.name: Accessory nerve (XI) (right)
nervous.description: The accessory nerve is a cranial nerve that supplies the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles.

nervous.name: Accessory nucleus of oculomotor nerve (left)
nervous.description: The fibers of the oculomotor nerve arise from a nucleus in the midbrain, which lies in the gray substance of the floor of the cerebral aqueduct and extends in front of the aqueduct for a short distance into the floor of the third ventricle.

nervous.name: Accessory nucleus of oculomotor nerve (right)
nervous.description: The fibers of the oculomotor nerve arise from a nucleus in the midbrain, which lies in the gray substance of the floor of the cerebral aqueduct and extends in front of the aqueduct for a short distance into the floor of the third ventricle.

nervous.name: Amygdaloid body (left)
nervous.description: The amygdala (plural: amygdalae or amygdalas; also corpus amygdaloideum; Latin from Greek, ἀμυγδαλή, amygdalē, 'almond', 'tonsil') is one of two almond-shaped clusters of nuclei located deep and medially within the temporal lobes of the brain's cerebrum in complex vertebrates, including humans.

nervous.name: Amygdaloid body (right)
nervous.description: The amygdala (plural: amygdalae or amygdalas; also corpus amygdaloideum; Latin from Greek, ἀμυγδαλή, amygdalē, 'almond', 'tonsil') is one of two almond-shaped clusters of nuclei located deep and medially within the temporal lobes of the brain's cerebrum in complex vertebrates, including humans.

nervous.name: Angular gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The angular gyrus is a region of the brain lying mainly in the anterolateral region of parietal lobe, that lies near the superior edge of the temporal lobe, and immediately posterior to the supramarginal gyrus.

nervous.name: Angular gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The angular gyrus is a region of the brain lying mainly in the anterolateral region of parietal lobe, that lies near the superior edge of the temporal lobe, and immediately posterior to the supramarginal gyrus.

nervous.name: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The volar branch (ramus volaris; anterior branch), the larger, passes usually in front of, but occasionally behind, the vena mediana cubiti (median basilic vein).

nervous.name: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The volar branch (ramus volaris; anterior branch), the larger, passes usually in front of, but occasionally behind, the vena mediana cubiti (median basilic vein).

nervous.name: Anterior branch of obturator nerve (left)

nervous.name: Anterior branch of obturator nerve (right)
nervous.description: The anterior branch of the obturator nerve is a branch of the obturator nerve found in the pelvis and leg.

nervous.name: Anterior chamber of eyeball (left)
nervous.description: The anterior chamber (AC) is the aqueous humor-filled space inside the eye between the iris and the cornea's innermost surface, the endothelium.

nervous.name: Anterior chamber of eyeball (right)
nervous.description: The anterior chamber (AC) is the aqueous humor-filled space inside the eye between the iris and the cornea's innermost surface, the endothelium.

nervous.name: Anterior cochlear nucleus (left)
nervous.description: The cochlear nuclear (CN) complex comprises two cranial nerve nuclei in the human brainstem, the ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) and the dorsal cochlear nucleus (DCN).

nervous.name: Anterior cochlear nucleus (right)
nervous.description: The cochlear nuclear (CN) complex comprises two cranial nerve nuclei in the human brainstem, the ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) and the dorsal cochlear nucleus (DCN).

nervous.name: Anterior commissure
nervous.description: The anterior commissure (also known as the precommissure) is a white matter tract (a bundle of axons) connecting the two temporal lobes of the cerebral hemispheres across the midline, and placed in front of the columns of the fornix.

nervous.name: Anterior corticospinal tract
nervous.description: The anterior corticospinal tract (also called the ventral corticospinal tract, "Bundle of Turck", medial corticospinal tract, direct pyramidal tract, or anterior cerebrospinal fasciculus) is a small bundle of descending fibers that connect the cerebral cortex to the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Anterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: The anterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks of brachial plexus innervate the flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Anterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: The anterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks of brachial plexus innervate the flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Anterior division of mandibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

nervous.name: Anterior division of mandibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

nervous.name: Anterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: The anterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks of brachial plexus innervate the flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Anterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: The anterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks of brachial plexus innervate the flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Anterior division of superior trunk of brachial plexus (left)

nervous.name: Anterior fasciculus proprius
nervous.description: The proper fasciculi, or spinospinal fasciculi, or propriospinal tracts, are groups of short fibres, ascending and descending, and crossed and uncrossed, within the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Anterior horn of spinal cord
nervous.description: The anterior grey column (also called the anterior cornu, anterior horn of spinal cord, motor horn or ventral horn) is the front column of grey matter in the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Anterior interosseous nerve of forearm (left)
nervous.description: The anterior interosseous nerve (volar interosseous nerve) is a branch of the median nerve that supplies the deep muscles on the anterior of the forearm, except the ulnar (medial) half of the flexor digitorum profundus.

nervous.name: Anterior interosseous nerve of forearm (right)
nervous.description: The anterior interosseous nerve (volar interosseous nerve) is a branch of the median nerve that supplies the deep muscles on the anterior of the forearm, except the ulnar (medial) half of the flexor digitorum profundus.

nervous.name: Anterior root of spinal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The anterior root of spinal nerve, or ventral root, or motor root, is the efferent motor root of a spinal nerve.

nervous.name: Anterior root of spinal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The anterior root of spinal nerve, or ventral root, or motor root, is the efferent motor root of a spinal nerve.

nervous.name: Anterior segment of eyeball (left)
nervous.description: The anterior segment or anterior cavity is the front third of the eye that includes the structures in front of the vitreous humour: the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens.

nervous.name: Anterior segment of eyeball (right)
nervous.description: The anterior segment or anterior cavity is the front third of the eye that includes the structures in front of the vitreous humour: the cornea, iris, ciliary body, and lens.

nervous.name: Anterior spinocerebellar tract
nervous.description: The ventral spinocerebellar tract (or anterior spinocerebellar tract) conveys proprioceptive information from the body to the cerebellum.

nervous.name: Anterior spinothalamic tract
nervous.description: The anterior spinothalamic tract, (Latin: tractus spinothalamicus anterior) or ventral spinothalamic fasciculus situated in the marginal part of the anterior funiculus and intermingled more or less with the vestibulospinal tract, is derived from cells in the posterior column or intermediate gray matter of the opposite side.

nervous.name: Auditory tube (left)
nervous.description: In anatomy, the Eustachian tube, also known as the auditory tube or pharyngotympanic tube, is a tube that links the nasopharynx to the middle ear, of which it is also a part.

nervous.name: Auditory tube (right)
nervous.description: In anatomy, the Eustachian tube, also known as the auditory tube or pharyngotympanic tube, is a tube that links the nasopharynx to the middle ear, of which it is also a part.

nervous.name: Axillary nerve (left)
nervous.description: The axillary nerve or the circumflex nerve is a nerve of the human body, that originates from the brachial plexus (upper trunk, posterior division, posterior cord) at the level of the axilla (armpit) and carries nerve fibers from C5 and C6.

nervous.name: Axillary nerve (right)
nervous.description: The axillary nerve or the circumflex nerve is a nerve of the human body, that originates from the brachial plexus (upper trunk, posterior division, posterior cord) at the level of the axilla (armpit) and carries nerve fibers from C5 and C6.

nervous.name: Buccal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The buccal nerve (long buccal nerve) is a nerve in the face.

nervous.name: Buccal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The buccal nerve (long buccal nerve) is a nerve in the face.

nervous.name: Calcarine sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The calcarine sulcus (or calcarine fissure) is an anatomical landmark located at the caudal end of the medial surface of the brain of humans and other primates.

nervous.name: Calcarine sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The calcarine sulcus (or calcarine fissure) is an anatomical landmark located at the caudal end of the medial surface of the brain of humans and other primates.

nervous.name: Cauda equina
nervous.description: The cauda equina (from Latin horse's tail) is a bundle of spinal nerves and spinal nerve rootlets, consisting of the second through fifth lumbar nerve pairs, the first through fifth sacral nerve pairs, and the coccygeal nerve, all of which arise from the lumbar enlargement and the conus medullaris of the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Caudate nucleus (left)
nervous.description: The caudate nucleus is one of the structures that make up the corpus striatum, which is a component of the basal ganglia.

nervous.name: Caudate nucleus (right)
nervous.description: The caudate nucleus is one of the structures that make up the corpus striatum, which is a component of the basal ganglia.

nervous.name: Central canal
nervous.description: The central canal (also known as ependymal canal) is the cerebrospinal fluid-filled space that runs through the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Central lobule
nervous.description: The central lobule is a small square lobule, situated in the anterior cerebellar notch.

nervous.name: Central sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The central sulcus is a sulcus, or groove, in the cerebral cortex in the brains of vertebrates.

nervous.name: Central sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The central sulcus is a sulcus, or groove, in the cerebral cortex in the brains of vertebrates.

nervous.name: Chorda tympani (left)
nervous.description: The chorda tympani is a branch of the facial nerve that originates from the taste buds in the front of the tongue, runs through the middle ear, and carries taste messages to the brain.

nervous.name: Chorda tympani (right)
nervous.description: The chorda tympani is a branch of the facial nerve that originates from the taste buds in the front of the tongue, runs through the middle ear, and carries taste messages to the brain.

nervous.name: Choroid plexus (left)

nervous.name: Choroid plexus (right)
nervous.description: The choroid plexus, or plica choroidea, is a plexus of cells that arises from the tela choroidea in each of the ventricles of the brain.

nervous.name: Circular sulcus of insula (left)
nervous.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

nervous.name: Circular sulcus of insula (right)
nervous.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

nervous.name: Cochlea (left)
nervous.description: The cochlea is the part of the inner ear involved in hearing.

nervous.name: Cochlea (right)
nervous.description: The cochlea is the part of the inner ear involved in hearing.

nervous.name: Cochlear nerve
nervous.description: The cochlear nerve (also auditory nerve or acoustic nerve) is one of two parts of the vestibulocochlear nerve, a cranial nerve present in amniotes, the other part being the vestibular nerve.

nervous.name: Cochlear nerve (left)
nervous.description: The cochlear nerve (also auditory nerve or acoustic nerve) is one of two parts of the vestibulocochlear nerve, a cranial nerve present in amniotes, the other part being the vestibular nerve.

nervous.name: Collateral sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The collateral fissure (or sulcus) is on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere and extends from near the occipital pole to within a short distance of the temporal pole.

nervous.name: Collateral sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The collateral fissure (or sulcus) is on the tentorial surface of the hemisphere and extends from near the occipital pole to within a short distance of the temporal pole.

nervous.name: Common fibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The common fibular nerve (also referred to as the common peroneal nerve, external popliteal nerve, or lateral popliteal nerve) is a nerve in the lower leg that provides sensation over the posterolateral part of the leg and the knee joint.

nervous.name: Common fibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The common fibular nerve (also referred to as the common peroneal nerve, external popliteal nerve, or lateral popliteal nerve) is a nerve in the lower leg that provides sensation over the posterolateral part of the leg and the knee joint.

nervous.name: Common palmar digital branches of median nerve (left)
nervous.description: In the palm of the hand the median nerve is covered by the skin and the palmar aponeurosis, and rests on the tendons of the Flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Common palmar digital branches of median nerve (right)
nervous.description: In the palm of the hand the median nerve is covered by the skin and the palmar aponeurosis, and rests on the tendons of the Flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Common palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The common palmar digital nerves of the ulnar nerve are nerves of the hand.

nervous.name: Common palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The common palmar digital nerves of the ulnar nerve are nerves of the hand.

nervous.name: Common plantar digital branches of lateral plantar nerve (left)
nervous.description: Two branches, of which one goes to the fifth toe, the other to the space between the fourth and fifth toe.

nervous.name: Common plantar digital branches of lateral plantar nerve (right)
nervous.description: Two branches, of which one goes to the fifth toe, the other to the space between the fourth and fifth toe.

nervous.name: Common plantar digital branches of medial plantar nerve
nervous.description: The common plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve are nerves of the foot.

nervous.name: Common plantar digital branches of medial plantar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The common plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve are nerves of the foot.

nervous.name: Cornea (left)
nervous.description: The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

nervous.name: Cornea (right)
nervous.description: The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris, pupil, and anterior chamber.

nervous.name: Corpus callosum
nervous.description: The corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain.

nervous.name: Culmen
nervous.description: A culmen is a top, a summit or a culminating point.

nervous.name: Cuneate fasciculus
nervous.description: The cuneate fasciculus is triangular on transverse section, and lies between the gracile fasciculus and the posterior column, its base corresponding with the surface of the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Cuneus (left)
nervous.description: The cuneus (Latin for "wedge"; plural, cunei) is a smaller lobe in the occipital lobe of the brain.

nervous.name: Cuneus (right)
nervous.description: The cuneus (Latin for "wedge"; plural, cunei) is a smaller lobe in the occipital lobe of the brain.

nervous.name: Deep branch of radial nerve (left)
nervous.description: The radial nerve divides into a superficial (sensory) and deep (motor) branch at the cubital fossa.

nervous.name: Deep branch of radial nerve (right)
nervous.description: The radial nerve divides into a superficial (sensory) and deep (motor) branch at the cubital fossa.

nervous.name: Deep branch of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The deep branch of the ulnar nerve is a terminal, primarily motor branch of the ulnar nerve.

nervous.name: Deep branch of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The deep branch of the ulnar nerve is a terminal, primarily motor branch of the ulnar nerve.

nervous.name: Deep fibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The deep fibular nerve, sometimes called the deep peroneal nerve, begins at the bifurcation of the common fibular nerve between the fibula and upper part of the peroneus longus, passes infero-medially, deep to extensor digitorum longus, to the anterior surface of the interosseous membrane, and comes into relation with the anterior tibial artery above the middle of the leg; it then descends with the artery to the front of the ankle-joint, where it divides into a lateral and a medial terminal branch.

nervous.name: Deep fibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The deep fibular nerve, sometimes called the deep peroneal nerve, begins at the bifurcation of the common fibular nerve between the fibula and upper part of the peroneus longus, passes infero-medially, deep to extensor digitorum longus, to the anterior surface of the interosseous membrane, and comes into relation with the anterior tibial artery above the middle of the leg; it then descends with the artery to the front of the ankle-joint, where it divides into a lateral and a medial terminal branch.

nervous.name: Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The dorsal branch of ulnar nerve arises about 5 cm.

nervous.name: Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The dorsal branch of ulnar nerve arises about 5 cm.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of deep fibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: Sensitive branches of the deep fibular nerve for the faces towards the hallux and the second toe.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of deep fibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: Sensitive branches of the deep fibular nerve for the faces towards the hallux and the second toe.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of radial nerve (left)
nervous.description: Dorsal digital nerves of radial nerve are branches on the dorsum of the hand.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of radial nerve (right)
nervous.description: Dorsal digital nerves of radial nerve are branches on the dorsum of the hand.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of superficial fibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: BRanches of the superficial fibular nerve for the toes, except the distal phalanges.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of superficial fibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: BRanches of the superficial fibular nerve for the toes, except the distal phalanges.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: Dorsal digital nerves of ulnar nerve are branches on the dorsum of the hand.

nervous.name: Dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: Dorsal digital nerves of ulnar nerve are branches on the dorsum of the hand.

nervous.name: Dorsal scapular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The dorsal scapular nerve is a branch of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Dorsal scapular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The dorsal scapular nerve is a branch of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Facial nerve (VII) (left)
nervous.description: The facial nerve (the labyrinthine segment) is the seventh cranial nerve, or simply CN VII.

nervous.name: Facial nerve (VII) (right)
nervous.description: The facial nerve (the labyrinthine segment) is the seventh cranial nerve, or simply CN VII.

nervous.name: Falx cerebri
nervous.description: The falx cerebri, also known as the cerebral falx, is a large, crescent-shaped fold of meningeal layer of dura mater that descends vertically in the longitudinal fissure between the cerebral hemispheres of the human brain.

nervous.name: Femoral branch of genitofemoral nerve (left)
nervous.description: The femoral branch passes underneath the inguinal ligament, travelling through the lateral muscular compartment of the femoral canal where it innervates skin of the upper leg.

nervous.name: Femoral branch of genitofemoral nerve (right)
nervous.description: The femoral branch passes underneath the inguinal ligament, travelling through the lateral muscular compartment of the femoral canal where it innervates skin of the upper leg.

nervous.name: Femoral nerve (left)
nervous.description: The femoral nerve is a nerve in the thigh that supplies skin on the upper thigh and inner leg, and the muscles that extend the knee.

nervous.name: Femoral nerve (right)
nervous.description: The femoral nerve is a nerve in the thigh that supplies skin on the upper thigh and inner leg, and the muscles that extend the knee.

nervous.name: Flocculus (left)
nervous.description: The flocculus (Latin: tuft of wool, diminutive) is a small lobe of the cerebellum at the posterior border of the middle cerebellar peduncle anterior to the biventer lobule.

nervous.name: Flocculus (right)
nervous.description: The flocculus (Latin: tuft of wool, diminutive) is a small lobe of the cerebellum at the posterior border of the middle cerebellar peduncle anterior to the biventer lobule.

nervous.name: Fornix (left)
nervous.description: The fornix (meaning "arch" in Latin) is a C-shaped bundle of nerve fibers in the brain that acts as the major output tract of the hippocampus.

nervous.name: Fornix (right)
nervous.description: The fornix (meaning "arch" in Latin) is a C-shaped bundle of nerve fibers in the brain that acts as the major output tract of the hippocampus.

nervous.name: Fourth ventricle
nervous.description: The fourth ventricle is one of the four connected fluid-filled cavities within the human brain.

nervous.name: Ganglia of sympathetic trunk (left)
nervous.description: The sympathetic ganglia, or paravertebral ganglia are autonomic ganglia, of the sympathetic nervous system.

nervous.name: Ganglia of sympathetic trunk (right)
nervous.description: The sympathetic ganglia, or paravertebral ganglia are autonomic ganglia, of the sympathetic nervous system.

nervous.name: Genital branch of genitofemoral nerve (left)
nervous.description: The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve, also known as the external spermatic nerve in males, is a nerve in the abdomen that arises from the genitofemoral nerve.

nervous.name: Genital branch of genitofemoral nerve (right)
nervous.description: The genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve, also known as the external spermatic nerve in males, is a nerve in the abdomen that arises from the genitofemoral nerve.

nervous.name: Genitofemoral nerve (left)
nervous.description: The genitofemoral nerve refers to a nerve that is found in the abdomen.

nervous.name: Genitofemoral nerve (right)
nervous.description: The genitofemoral nerve refers to a nerve that is found in the abdomen.

nervous.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) (left)
nervous.description: The glossopharyngeal nerve, known as the ninth cranial nerve (CN IX), is a mixed nerve that carries afferent sensory and efferent motor information.

nervous.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX) (right)
nervous.description: The glossopharyngeal nerve, known as the ninth cranial nerve (CN IX), is a mixed nerve that carries afferent sensory and efferent motor information.

nervous.name: Gracile fasciculus
nervous.description: The gracile fasciculus carries sensory information from the lower half of the body entering the spinal cord at the lumbar level.

nervous.name: Habenula
nervous.description: In neuroanatomy, habenula (diminutive of Latin habena meaning rein) originally denoted the stalk of the pineal gland (pineal habenula; pedunculus of pineal body), but gradually came to refer to a neighboring group of nerve cells with which the pineal gland was believed to be associated, the habenular nucleus.

nervous.name: Hippocampal commissure
nervous.description: The lateral portions of the body of the fornix are joined by a thin triangular lamina, named the psalterium (lyra).

nervous.name: Hippocampus (left)
nervous.description: The hippocampus (via Latin from Greek ἱππόκαμπος, 'seahorse') is a major component of the brain of humans and other vertebrates.

nervous.name: Hippocampus (right)
nervous.description: The hippocampus (via Latin from Greek ἱππόκαμπος, 'seahorse') is a major component of the brain of humans and other vertebrates.

nervous.name: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) (left)
nervous.description: The hypoglossal nerve is the twelfth cranial nerve, and innervates all the extrinsic and intrinsic muscles of the tongue, except for the palatoglossus which is innervated by the vagus nerve.

nervous.name: Hypoglossal nerve (XII) (right)
nervous.description: The hypoglossal nerve is the twelfth cranial nerve, and innervates all the extrinsic and intrinsic muscles of the tongue, except for the palatoglossus which is innervated by the vagus nerve.

nervous.name: Hypothalamus
nervous.description: The hypothalamus (from Ancient Greek ὑπό (hupó) 'under', and θάλαμος (thálamos) 'chamber') is a portion of the brain that contains a number of small nuclei with a variety of functions.

nervous.name: Ilio-inguinal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The ilio-inguinal nerve is a branch of the first lumbar nerve (L1).

nervous.name: Ilio-inguinal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The ilio-inguinal nerve is a branch of the first lumbar nerve (L1).

nervous.name: Iliohypogastric nerve (left)
nervous.description: The iliohypogastric nerve is a nerve that originates from the lumbar plexus that supplies sensation to skin over the lateral gluteal and hypogastric regions and motor to the internal oblique muscles and transverse abdominal muscles.

nervous.name: Iliohypogastric nerve (right)
nervous.description: The iliohypogastric nerve is a nerve that originates from the lumbar plexus that supplies sensation to skin over the lateral gluteal and hypogastric regions and motor to the internal oblique muscles and transverse abdominal muscles.

nervous.name: Inferior alveolar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The inferior alveolar nerve (sometimes called the inferior dental nerve) is a branch of the mandibular nerve, which is itself the third branch of the trigeminal nerve.

nervous.name: Inferior alveolar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The inferior alveolar nerve (sometimes called the inferior dental nerve) is a branch of the mandibular nerve, which is itself the third branch of the trigeminal nerve.

nervous.name: Inferior colliculus (left)
nervous.description: The inferior colliculus (IC) (Latin for lower hill) is the principal midbrain nucleus of the auditory pathway and receives input from several peripheral brainstem nuclei in the auditory pathway, as well as inputs from the auditory cortex.

nervous.name: Inferior colliculus (right)
nervous.description: The inferior colliculus (IC) (Latin for lower hill) is the principal midbrain nucleus of the auditory pathway and receives input from several peripheral brainstem nuclei in the auditory pathway, as well as inputs from the auditory cortex.

nervous.name: Inferior frontal sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The inferior frontal sulcus is a sulcus between the middle frontal gyrus and the inferior frontal gyrus.

nervous.name: Inferior frontal sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The inferior frontal sulcus is a sulcus between the middle frontal gyrus and the inferior frontal gyrus.

nervous.name: Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus* (left)
nervous.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain.

nervous.name: Inferior occipital gyrus and sulcus* (right)
nervous.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain.

nervous.name: Inferior salivatory nucleus (left)
nervous.description: The salivatory nuclei are the superior salivatory nucleus, and the inferior salivatory nucleus that innervate the salivary glands.

nervous.name: Inferior salivatory nucleus (right)
nervous.description: The salivatory nuclei are the superior salivatory nucleus, and the inferior salivatory nucleus that innervate the salivary glands.

nervous.name: Inferior temporal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The inferior temporal gyrus is one of three gyri of the temporal lobe and is located below the middle temporal gyrus, connected behind with the inferior occipital gyrus; it also extends around the infero-lateral border on to the inferior surface of the temporal lobe, where it is limited by the inferior sulcus.

nervous.name: Inferior temporal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The inferior temporal gyrus is one of three gyri of the temporal lobe and is located below the middle temporal gyrus, connected behind with the inferior occipital gyrus; it also extends around the infero-lateral border on to the inferior surface of the temporal lobe, where it is limited by the inferior sulcus.

nervous.name: Inferior temporal sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The inferior surface of the temporal lobe is concave, and is continuous posteriorly with the tentorial surface of the occipital lobe.

nervous.name: Inferior temporal sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The inferior surface of the temporal lobe is concave, and is continuous posteriorly with the tentorial surface of the occipital lobe.

nervous.name: Inferior trunk of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: ==Trunks==

nervous.name: Inferior trunk of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: ==Trunks==

nervous.name: Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. and post. sulci*) (left)
nervous.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

nervous.name: Insula (Subcentral gyrus and ant. and post. sulci*) (right)
nervous.description: The insular cortex (also insula and insular lobe) is a portion of the cerebral cortex folded deep within the lateral sulcus (the fissure separating the temporal lobe from the parietal and frontal lobes) within each hemisphere of the mammalian brain.

nervous.name: Intercostal nerves (left)
nervous.description: The intercostal nerves are part of the somatic nervous system, and arise from the anterior rami of the thoracic spinal nerves from T1 to T11.

nervous.name: Intercostal nerves (right)
nervous.description: The intercostal nerves are part of the somatic nervous system, and arise from the anterior rami of the thoracic spinal nerves from T1 to T11.

nervous.name: Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot (left)
nervous.description: The intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve (external dorsal cutaneous branch), the smaller, passes along the lateral part of the dorsum of the foot, and divides into dorsal digital branches, which supply the contiguous sides of the third and fourth, and of the fourth and fifth toes.

nervous.name: Intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot (right)
nervous.description: The intermediate dorsal cutaneous nerve (external dorsal cutaneous branch), the smaller, passes along the lateral part of the dorsum of the foot, and divides into dorsal digital branches, which supply the contiguous sides of the third and fourth, and of the fourth and fifth toes.

nervous.name: Intermediolateral nucleus
nervous.description: The intermediolateral nucleus (IML) is a region of grey matter found in one of the three grey columns of the spinal cord, the lateral grey column.

nervous.name: Interpeduncular fossa (left)
nervous.description: The interpeduncular fossa is a somewhat rhomboid-shaped area of the base of the brain, limited in front by the optic chiasma, behind by the antero-superior surface of the pons, antero-laterally by the converging optic tracts, and postero-laterally by the diverging cerebral peduncles.

nervous.name: Interpeduncular fossa (right)
nervous.description: The interpeduncular fossa is a somewhat rhomboid-shaped area of the base of the brain, limited in front by the optic chiasma, behind by the antero-superior surface of the pons, antero-laterally by the converging optic tracts, and postero-laterally by the diverging cerebral peduncles.

nervous.name: Intraparietal sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The intraparietal sulcus (IPS) is located on the lateral surface of the parietal lobe, and consists of an oblique and a horizontal portion.

nervous.name: Intraparietal sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The intraparietal sulcus (IPS) is located on the lateral surface of the parietal lobe, and consists of an oblique and a horizontal portion.

nervous.name: Iris (left)
nervous.description: In humans and most mammals and birds, the iris (plural: irides or irises) is a thin, annular structure in the eye, responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, thus the amount of light reaching the retina.

nervous.name: Iris (right)
nervous.description: In humans and most mammals and birds, the iris (plural: irides or irises) is a thin, annular structure in the eye, responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, thus the amount of light reaching the retina.

nervous.name: Lacrimal canaliculus (left)
nervous.description: The lacrimal canaliculi, (sing. canaliculus), are the small channels in each eyelid that drain lacrimal fluid, from the lacrimal puncta to the lacrimal sac.

nervous.name: Lacrimal canaliculus (right)
nervous.description: The lacrimal canaliculi, (sing. canaliculus), are the small channels in each eyelid that drain lacrimal fluid, from the lacrimal puncta to the lacrimal sac.

nervous.name: Lacrimal gland (left)
nervous.description: The lacrimal glands are paired exocrine glands, one for each eye, found in most terrestrial vertebrates and some marine mammals, that secrete the aqueous layer of the tear film.

nervous.name: Lacrimal gland (right)
nervous.description: The lacrimal glands are paired exocrine glands, one for each eye, found in most terrestrial vertebrates and some marine mammals, that secrete the aqueous layer of the tear film.

nervous.name: Lacrimal sac (left)
nervous.description: The lacrimal sac or lachrymal sac is the upper dilated end of the nasolacrimal duct, and is lodged in a deep groove formed by the lacrimal bone and frontal process of the maxilla.

nervous.name: Lacrimal sac (right)
nervous.description: The lacrimal sac or lachrymal sac is the upper dilated end of the nasolacrimal duct, and is lodged in a deep groove formed by the lacrimal bone and frontal process of the maxilla.

nervous.name: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (or lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm) (branch of musculocutaneous nerve, also sometimes spelled "antebrachial") passes behind the cephalic vein, and divides, opposite the elbow-joint, into a volar and a dorsal branch.

nervous.name: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve (or lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm) (branch of musculocutaneous nerve, also sometimes spelled "antebrachial") passes behind the cephalic vein, and divides, opposite the elbow-joint, into a volar and a dorsal branch.

nervous.name: Lateral corticospinal tract
nervous.description: The lateral corticospinal tract (also called the crossed pyramidal tract or lateral cerebrospinal fasciculus) is the largest part of the corticospinal tract.

nervous.name: Lateral fasciculus proprius
nervous.description: The proper fasciculi, or spinospinal fasciculi, or propriospinal tracts, are groups of short fibres, ascending and descending, and crossed and uncrossed, within the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh (also called the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve) is a cutaneous nerve of the thigh.

nervous.name: Lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh (also called the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve) is a cutaneous nerve of the thigh.

nervous.name: Lateral geniculate body (left)
nervous.description: The lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN; also called the lateral geniculate body or lateral geniculate complex) is a relay center in the thalamus for the visual pathway.

nervous.name: Lateral geniculate body (right)
nervous.description: The lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN; also called the lateral geniculate body or lateral geniculate complex) is a relay center in the thalamus for the visual pathway.

nervous.name: Lateral intermediate substance
nervous.description: The lateral grey column (lateral column, lateral cornu, lateral horn of spinal cord, intermediolateral column) is one of the three grey columns of the spinal cord (which give the shape of a butterfly); the others being the anterior and posterior grey columns.

nervous.name: Lateral occipital gyrus (Middle occipital gyrus*) (left)
nervous.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain.

nervous.name: Lateral occipital gyrus (Middle occipital gyrus*) (right)
nervous.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain.

nervous.name: Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The fusiform gyrus, also known as the lateral occipitotemporal gyrus, is part of the temporal lobe and occipital lobe in Brodmann area 37.

nervous.name: Lateral occipitotemporal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The fusiform gyrus, also known as the lateral occipitotemporal gyrus, is part of the temporal lobe and occipital lobe in Brodmann area 37.

nervous.name: Lateral pectoral nerve (left)
nervous.description: The lateral pectoral nerve (also known as the lateral anterior thoracic nerve) arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, and through it from the C5-7.

nervous.name: Lateral pectoral nerve (right)
nervous.description: The lateral pectoral nerve (also known as the lateral anterior thoracic nerve) arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, and through it from the C5-7.

nervous.name: Lateral plantar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The lateral plantar nerve (external plantar nerve) is a branch of the tibial nerve, in turn a branch of the sciatic nerve and supplies the skin of the fifth toe and lateral half of the fourth, as well as most of the deep muscles, its distribution being similar to that of the ulnar nerve in the hand.

nervous.name: Lateral plantar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The lateral plantar nerve (external plantar nerve) is a branch of the tibial nerve, in turn a branch of the sciatic nerve and supplies the skin of the fifth toe and lateral half of the fourth, as well as most of the deep muscles, its distribution being similar to that of the ulnar nerve in the hand.

nervous.name: Lateral reticulospinal tract
nervous.description: The medial reticular formation and lateral reticular formation are two columns of nuclei with ill-defined boundaries that send projections through the medulla and into the midbrain.

nervous.name: Lateral spinothalamic tract
nervous.description: The lateral spinothalamic tract (or lateral spinothalamic fasciculus), is a bundle of afferent nerve fibers ascending through the white matter of the spinal cord, in the spinothalamic tract, carrying sensory information to the brain.

nervous.name: Lateral ventricle (left)
nervous.description: The lateral ventricles are the two largest ventricles of the brain and contain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

nervous.name: Lateral ventricle (right)
nervous.description: The lateral ventricles are the two largest ventricles of the brain and contain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).

nervous.name: Lateral vestibulospinal tract
nervous.description: The lateral vestibulospinal tract is one of the descending spinal tracts of the ventromedial funiculus. The lateral part of the vestibulospinal tract is the major portion and is composed of fibers originating in the lateral, superior, and inferior vestibular nuclei (primarily the lateral).

nervous.name: Lens (left)
nervous.description: The lens is a transparent biconvex structure in the eye that, along with the cornea, helps to refract light to be focused on the retina.

nervous.name: Lens (right)
nervous.description: The lens is a transparent biconvex structure in the eye that, along with the cornea, helps to refract light to be focused on the retina.

nervous.name: Lingual nerve (left)
nervous.description: The lingual nerve carries sensory innervation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

nervous.name: Lingual nerve (right)
nervous.description: The lingual nerve carries sensory innervation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.

nervous.name: Lingula of cerebellum
nervous.description: The lingula is a small tongue-shaped process, consisting of four or five folia; it lies in front of the lobulus centralis, and is concealed by it.
