Anteriorly, it rests on the dorsal surface of the anterior medullary velum, and its white substance is continuous with that of the velum.

nervous.name: Long thoracic nerve (left)
nervous.description: The long thoracic nerve (external respiratory nerve of Bell; posterior thoracic nerve) innervates the serratus anterior muscle.

nervous.name: Long thoracic nerve (right)
nervous.description: The long thoracic nerve (external respiratory nerve of Bell; posterior thoracic nerve) innervates the serratus anterior muscle.

nervous.name: Lunate sulcus (left)
nervous.description: In brain anatomy, the lunate sulcus or simian sulcus also known as the sulcus lunatus is a fissure in the occipital lobe variably found in humans and more often larger when present in apes and monkeys.

nervous.name: Lunate sulcus (right)
nervous.description: In brain anatomy, the lunate sulcus or simian sulcus also known as the sulcus lunatus is a fissure in the occipital lobe variably found in humans and more often larger when present in apes and monkeys.

nervous.name: Maxillary nerve (left)
nervous.description: The maxillary nerve (V2) is one of the three branches or divisions of the trigeminal nerve, the fifth (CN V) cranial nerve.

nervous.name: Maxillary nerve (right)
nervous.description: The maxillary nerve (V2) is one of the three branches or divisions of the trigeminal nerve, the fifth (CN V) cranial nerve.

nervous.name: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm (medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve) branches from the medial cord of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm (medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve) branches from the medial cord of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Medial brachial cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The medial brachial cutaneous nerve (lesser internal cutaneous nerve; medial cutaneous nerve of arm) is distributed to the skin on the medial brachial side of the arm.

nervous.name: Medial brachial cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The medial brachial cutaneous nerve (lesser internal cutaneous nerve; medial cutaneous nerve of arm) is distributed to the skin on the medial brachial side of the arm.

nervous.name: Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot (left)
nervous.description: The medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot passes in front of the ankle-joint, and divides into two dorsal digital branches, one of which supplies the medial side of the great toe, the other, the adjacent side of the second and third toes.

nervous.name: Medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot (right)
nervous.description: The medial dorsal cutaneous nerve of foot passes in front of the ankle-joint, and divides into two dorsal digital branches, one of which supplies the medial side of the great toe, the other, the adjacent side of the second and third toes.

nervous.name: Medial geniculate body (left)
nervous.description: The medial geniculate nucleus (MGN) or medial geniculate body (MGB) is part of the auditory thalamus and represents the thalamic relay between the inferior colliculus (IC) and the auditory cortex (AC).

nervous.name: Medial geniculate body (right)
nervous.description: The medial geniculate nucleus (MGN) or medial geniculate body (MGB) is part of the auditory thalamus and represents the thalamic relay between the inferior colliculus (IC) and the auditory cortex (AC).

nervous.name: Medial occipitotemporal gyrus (Parahippocampal*) (left)
nervous.description: The parahippocampal gyrus (or hippocampal gyrus) is a grey matter cortical region of the brain that surrounds the hippocampus and is part of the limbic system.

nervous.name: Medial occipitotemporal gyrus (Parahippocampal*) (right)
nervous.description: The parahippocampal gyrus (or hippocampal gyrus) is a grey matter cortical region of the brain that surrounds the hippocampus and is part of the limbic system.

nervous.name: Medial plantar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The medial plantar nerve (internal plantar nerve) is the larger of the two terminal divisions of the tibial nerve (medial and lateral plantar nerve), which accompanies the medial plantar artery.

nervous.name: Medial plantar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The medial plantar nerve (internal plantar nerve) is the larger of the two terminal divisions of the tibial nerve (medial and lateral plantar nerve), which accompanies the medial plantar artery.

nervous.name: Medial reticulospinal tract
nervous.description: The medial reticular formation and lateral reticular formation are two columns of nuclei with ill-defined boundaries that send projections through the medulla and into the midbrain.

nervous.name: Medial sural cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The medial sural cutaneous nerve is a sensory nerve of the leg. It supplies part of the medial side of the leg.

nervous.name: Medial sural cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The medial sural cutaneous nerve is a sensory nerve of the leg. It supplies part of the medial side of the leg.

nervous.name: Medial vestibulospinal tract
nervous.description: The medial vestibulospinal tract is one of the descending spinal tracts of the ventromedial funiculus of the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Median nerve (left)
nervous.description: The median nerve is a nerve in humans and other animals in the upper limb.

nervous.name: Median nerve (right)
nervous.description: The median nerve is a nerve in humans and other animals in the upper limb.

nervous.name: Medulla oblongata (left)
nervous.description: The medulla oblongata or simply medulla is a long stem-like structure which makes up the lower part of the brainstem.

nervous.name: Medulla oblongata (right)
nervous.description: The medulla oblongata or simply medulla is a long stem-like structure which makes up the lower part of the brainstem.

nervous.name: Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve (left)
nervous.description: MENINGEAL BRANCH OF MAXILLARY NERVE/ MENINGEAL BRANCH OF THE MANDIBULAR NERVE (to be verified)

nervous.name: Meningeal branch of maxillary nerve (right)
nervous.description: MENINGEAL BRANCH OF MAXILLARY NERVE/ MENINGEAL BRANCH OF THE MANDIBULAR NERVE (to be verified)

nervous.name: Mental nerve (left)
nervous.description: Mental nerve is a sensory nerve which provides sensation to the front of the chin and lower lip as well as the labial gingivae of the mandibular anterior teeth and the premolars.

nervous.name: Mental nerve (right)
nervous.description: Mental nerve is a sensory nerve which provides sensation to the front of the chin and lower lip as well as the labial gingivae of the mandibular anterior teeth and the premolars.

nervous.name: Midbrain (left)
nervous.description: The midbrain or mesencephalon is the forward-most portion of the brainstem and is associated with vision, hearing, motor control, sleep and wakefulness, arousal (alertness), and temperature regulation.

nervous.name: Midbrain (right)
nervous.description: The midbrain or mesencephalon is the forward-most portion of the brainstem and is associated with vision, hearing, motor control, sleep and wakefulness, arousal (alertness), and temperature regulation.

nervous.name: Middle frontal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The middle frontal gyrus makes up about one-third of the frontal lobe of the human brain. (A gyrus is one of the prominent "bumps" or "ridges" on the surface of the human brain.)

nervous.name: Middle frontal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The middle frontal gyrus makes up about one-third of the frontal lobe of the human brain. (A gyrus is one of the prominent "bumps" or "ridges" on the surface of the human brain.)

nervous.name: Middle temporal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: Middle temporal gyrus is a gyrus in the brain on the temporal lobe.

nervous.name: Middle temporal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: Middle temporal gyrus is a gyrus in the brain on the temporal lobe.

nervous.name: Middle trunk of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: ==Trunks==

nervous.name: Middle trunk of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: ==Trunks==

nervous.name: Motor nucleus of facial nerve (left)
nervous.description: The facial motor nucleus is a collection of neurons in the brainstem that belong to the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII).

nervous.name: Motor nucleus of facial nerve (right)
nervous.description: The facial motor nucleus is a collection of neurons in the brainstem that belong to the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII).

nervous.name: Motor root of trigeminal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The trigeminal motor nucleus contains motor neurons that innervate muscles of the first branchial arch, namely the muscles of mastication, the tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini, mylohyoid, and anterior belly of the digastric.

nervous.name: Motor root of trigeminal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The trigeminal motor nucleus contains motor neurons that innervate muscles of the first branchial arch, namely the muscles of mastication, the tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini, mylohyoid, and anterior belly of the digastric.

nervous.name: Muscular branches of deep fibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: Branches of the deep fibular nerve for the

nervous.name: Muscular branches of deep fibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: Branches of the deep fibular nerve for the

nervous.name: Muscular branches of radial nerve (left)
nervous.description: The muscular branches of the radial nerve supply the Triceps brachii, Anconæus, Brachioradialis, and Extensor carpi radialis longus, and are grouped as medial, posterior, and lateral.

nervous.name: Muscular branches of radial nerve (right)
nervous.description: The muscular branches of the radial nerve supply the Triceps brachii, Anconæus, Brachioradialis, and Extensor carpi radialis longus, and are grouped as medial, posterior, and lateral.

nervous.name: Muscular branches of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The muscular branches of ulnar nerve are a variety of branches of the ulnar nerve.

nervous.name: Muscular branches of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The muscular branches of ulnar nerve are a variety of branches of the ulnar nerve.

nervous.name: Musculocutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The musculocutaneous nerve arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, opposite the lower border of the pectoralis major, its fibers being derived from C5, C6 and C7.

nervous.name: Musculocutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The musculocutaneous nerve arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus, opposite the lower border of the pectoralis major, its fibers being derived from C5, C6 and C7.

nervous.name: Nasolacrimal duct (left)
nervous.description: The nasolacrimal duct (also called the tear duct) carries tears from the lacrimal sac of the eye into the nasal cavity.

nervous.name: Nasolacrimal duct (right)
nervous.description: The nasolacrimal duct (also called the tear duct) carries tears from the lacrimal sac of the eye into the nasal cavity.

nervous.name: Nodule of vermis
nervous.description: The nodule (nodular lobe), or anterior end of the inferior vermis, abuts against the roof of the fourth ventricle, and can only be distinctly seen after the cerebellum has been separated from the medulla oblongata and pons.

nervous.name: Nucleus ambiguus (left)
nervous.description: The nucleus ambiguus ("ambiguous nucleus" in English) is a group of large motor neurons, situated deep in the medullary reticular formation named by Jacob Clarke.

nervous.name: Nucleus ambiguus (right)
nervous.description: The nucleus ambiguus ("ambiguous nucleus" in English) is a group of large motor neurons, situated deep in the medullary reticular formation named by Jacob Clarke.

nervous.name: Nucleus of abducens nerve (left)
nervous.description: The abducens nucleus is the originating nucleus from which the abducens nerve (VI) emerges—a cranial nerve nucleus.

nervous.name: Nucleus of abducens nerve (right)
nervous.description: The abducens nucleus is the originating nucleus from which the abducens nerve (VI) emerges—a cranial nerve nucleus.

nervous.name: Nucleus of accessory nerve (left)
nervous.description: The spinal accessory nucleus lies within the cervical spinal cord (C1-C5) in the posterolateral aspect of the anterior horn.

nervous.name: Nucleus of accessory nerve (right)
nervous.description: The spinal accessory nucleus lies within the cervical spinal cord (C1-C5) in the posterolateral aspect of the anterior horn.

nervous.name: Nucleus of hypoglossal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The hypoglossal nucleus is a cranial nerve nucleus, found within the medulla.

nervous.name: Nucleus of hypoglossal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The hypoglossal nucleus is a cranial nerve nucleus, found within the medulla.

nervous.name: Nucleus of oculomotor nerve (left)
nervous.description: The fibers of the oculomotor nerve arise from a nucleus in the midbrain, which lies in the gray substance of the floor of the cerebral aqueduct and extends in front of the aqueduct for a short distance into the floor of the third ventricle.

nervous.name: Nucleus of oculomotor nerve (right)
nervous.description: The fibers of the oculomotor nerve arise from a nucleus in the midbrain, which lies in the gray substance of the floor of the cerebral aqueduct and extends in front of the aqueduct for a short distance into the floor of the third ventricle.

nervous.name: Nucleus of trochlear nerve (left)
nervous.description: The nucleus of the trochlear nerve  is located in the midbrain, at an intercollicular level between the superior colliculus and inferior colliculus.

nervous.name: Nucleus of trochlear nerve (right)
nervous.description: The nucleus of the trochlear nerve  is located in the midbrain, at an intercollicular level between the superior colliculus and inferior colliculus.

nervous.name: Nucleus proprius
nervous.description: The nucleus proprius is a layer of the spinal cord adjacent to the substantia gelatinosa.

nervous.name: Obturator nerve (left)
nervous.description: The obturator nerve in human anatomy arises from the ventral divisions of the second, third, and fourth lumbar nerves in the lumbar plexus; the branch from the third is the largest, while that from the second is often very small.

nervous.name: Obturator nerve (right)
nervous.description: The obturator nerve in human anatomy arises from the ventral divisions of the second, third, and fourth lumbar nerves in the lumbar plexus; the branch from the third is the largest, while that from the second is often very small.

nervous.name: Occipital pole (left)
nervous.description: There are three known poles of the cerebral hemispheres: the occipital pole, the frontal pole, and the temporal pole.

nervous.name: Occipital pole (right)
nervous.description: There are three known poles of the cerebral hemispheres: the occipital pole, the frontal pole, and the temporal pole.

nervous.name: Oculomotor nerve (III) (left)
nervous.description: The oculomotor nerve is the third cranial nerve (CN III).

nervous.name: Oculomotor nerve (III) (right)
nervous.description: The oculomotor nerve is the third cranial nerve (CN III).

nervous.name: Olfactory nerve (I) (left)
nervous.description: The olfactory nerve is typically considered the first cranial nerve, or simply CN I, that contains sensory nerve fibers relating to the sense of smell.

nervous.name: Olfactory nerve (I) (right)
nervous.description: The olfactory nerve is typically considered the first cranial nerve, or simply CN I, that contains sensory nerve fibers relating to the sense of smell.

nervous.name: Olfactory sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The olfactory tract is a bilateral bundle of afferent nerve fibers from the mitral and tufted cells of the olfactory bulb that connects to several target regions in the brain, including the piriform cortex, amygdala, and entorhinal cortex.

nervous.name: Olfactory sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The olfactory tract is a bilateral bundle of afferent nerve fibers from the mitral and tufted cells of the olfactory bulb that connects to several target regions in the brain, including the piriform cortex, amygdala, and entorhinal cortex.

nervous.name: Olive (left)
nervous.description: In anatomy, the olivary bodies or simply olives (Latin oliva and olivae, singular and plural, respectively) are a pair of prominent oval structures in the medulla oblongata, the lower portion of the brainstem.

nervous.name: Olive (right)
nervous.description: In anatomy, the olivary bodies or simply olives (Latin oliva and olivae, singular and plural, respectively) are a pair of prominent oval structures in the medulla oblongata, the lower portion of the brainstem.

nervous.name: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The inferior frontal gyrus is highly convoluted and has three cytoarchitecturally diverse regions.

nervous.name: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The inferior frontal gyrus is highly convoluted and has three cytoarchitecturally diverse regions.

nervous.name: Ophthalmic nerve (left)
nervous.description: The ophthalmic nerve (V1) is a sensory nerve of the face.

nervous.name: Ophthalmic nerve (right)
nervous.description: The ophthalmic nerve (V1) is a sensory nerve of the face.

nervous.name: Optic chiasm (left)
nervous.description: The optic chiasm, or optic chiasma is the part of the brain where the optic nerves cross.

nervous.name: Optic chiasm (right)
nervous.description: The optic chiasm, or optic chiasma is the part of the brain where the optic nerves cross.

nervous.name: Optic nerve (II) (left)
nervous.description: The optic nerve, also known as cranial nerve II, or simply as CN II, is a paired cranial nerve that transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.

nervous.name: Optic nerve (II) (right)
nervous.description: The optic nerve, also known as cranial nerve II, or simply as CN II, is a paired cranial nerve that transmits visual information from the retina to the brain.

nervous.name: Optic tract (left)
nervous.description: The optic tract (from the Latin tractus opticus) is a part of the visual system in the brain.

nervous.name: Optic tract (right)
nervous.description: The optic tract (from the Latin tractus opticus) is a part of the visual system in the brain.

nervous.name: Orbital gyri (Frontomarginal gyrus and sulcus*) (left)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Orbital gyri (Frontomarginal gyrus and sulcus*) (right)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Orbital gyri (left)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Orbital gyri (right)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Orbital part of  inferior frontal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: Orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus (pars orbitalis) (cortex inferior and anterior to the horizontal ramus of the lateral sulcus).

nervous.name: Orbital part of  inferior frontal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: Orbital part of inferior frontal gyrus (pars orbitalis) (cortex inferior and anterior to the horizontal ramus of the lateral sulcus).

nervous.name: Orbital sulci (H-shaped orbital sulci*) (left)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Orbital sulci (H-shaped orbital sulci*) (right)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Orbital sulci (Lateral Orbital sulcus*) (left)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Orbital sulci (Lateral Orbital sulcus*) (right)
nervous.description: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone.

nervous.name: Palmar branch of median nerve (left)
nervous.description: The palmar branch of the median nerve is a branch of the median nerve which arises at the distal part of the forearm.

nervous.name: Palmar branch of median nerve (right)
nervous.description: The palmar branch of the median nerve is a branch of the median nerve which arises at the distal part of the forearm.

nervous.name: Palmar branch of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The palmar branch of the ulnar nerve arises about five cm proximal to the wrist from where the ulnar nerve splits into palmar and dorsal branches.

nervous.name: Palmar branch of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The palmar branch of the ulnar nerve arises about five cm proximal to the wrist from where the ulnar nerve splits into palmar and dorsal branches.

nervous.name: Paracentral gyrus and sulcus* (left)
nervous.description: The paracentral sulcus is a sulcus of the brain.

nervous.name: Paracentral gyrus and sulcus* (right)
nervous.description: The paracentral sulcus is a sulcus of the brain.

nervous.name: Parieto-occipital sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The parieto-occipital sulcus (also called the parieto-occipital fissure) is a deep sulcus in the cerebral cortex that marks the boundary between the cuneus and precuneus, and also between the parietal and occipital lobes.

nervous.name: Parieto-occipital sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The parieto-occipital sulcus (also called the parieto-occipital fissure) is a deep sulcus in the cerebral cortex that marks the boundary between the cuneus and precuneus, and also between the parietal and occipital lobes.

nervous.name: Pons (left)
nervous.description: The pons (from Latin pons, "bridge") is part of the brainstem that in humans and other bipeds lies inferior to the midbrain, superior to the medulla oblongata and anterior to the cerebellum.

nervous.name: Pons (right)
nervous.description: The pons (from Latin pons, "bridge") is part of the brainstem that in humans and other bipeds lies inferior to the midbrain, superior to the medulla oblongata and anterior to the cerebellum.

nervous.name: Postcentral gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The postcentral gyrus is a prominent gyrus in the lateral parietal lobe of the human brain.

nervous.name: Postcentral gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The postcentral gyrus is a prominent gyrus in the lateral parietal lobe of the human brain.

nervous.name: Postcentral sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The postcentral sulcus of the parietal lobe lies parallel to, and behind, the central sulcus in the human brain.

nervous.name: Postcentral sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The postcentral sulcus of the parietal lobe lies parallel to, and behind, the central sulcus in the human brain.

nervous.name: Posterior antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The posterior cutaneous nerve of forearm is a nerve found in humans and other animals.

nervous.name: Posterior antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The posterior cutaneous nerve of forearm is a nerve found in humans and other animals.

nervous.name: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The ulnar branch (ramus ulnaris; posterior branch) passes obliquely downward on the medial side of the basilic vein, in front of the medial epicondyle of the humerus, to the back of the forearm, and descends on its ulnar side as far as the wrist, distributing filaments to the skin.

nervous.name: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The ulnar branch (ramus ulnaris; posterior branch) passes obliquely downward on the medial side of the basilic vein, in front of the medial epicondyle of the humerus, to the back of the forearm, and descends on its ulnar side as far as the wrist, distributing filaments to the skin.

nervous.name: Posterior branch of obturator nerve (left)
nervous.description: The posterior branch of the obturator nerve pierces the anterior part of the obturator externus, and supplies this muscle; it then passes behind the adductor brevis on the front of the adductor magnus, where it divides into numerous muscular branches which are distributed to the adductor magnus and the adductor brevis.

nervous.name: Posterior branch of obturator nerve (right)
nervous.description: The posterior branch of the obturator nerve pierces the anterior part of the obturator externus, and supplies this muscle; it then passes behind the adductor brevis on the front of the adductor magnus, where it divides into numerous muscular branches which are distributed to the adductor magnus and the adductor brevis.

nervous.name: Posterior cochlear nucleus (left)
nervous.description: The cochlear nuclear (CN) complex comprises two cranial nerve nuclei in the human brainstem, the ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) and the dorsal cochlear nucleus (DCN).

nervous.name: Posterior cochlear nucleus (right)
nervous.description: The cochlear nuclear (CN) complex comprises two cranial nerve nuclei in the human brainstem, the ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) and the dorsal cochlear nucleus (DCN).

nervous.name: Posterior commissure
nervous.description: The posterior commissure (also known as the epithalamic commissure) is a rounded band of white fibers crossing the middle line on the dorsal aspect of the rostral end of the cerebral aqueduct.

nervous.name: Posterior cord of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: The posterior cord is a part of the infraclavicular part of brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Posterior cord of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: The posterior cord is a part of the infraclavicular part of brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Posterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: The posterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks innervate the extensor muscles.

nervous.name: Posterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: The posterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks innervate the extensor muscles.

nervous.name: Posterior division of mandibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

nervous.name: Posterior division of mandibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The mandibular nerve divides into a small anterior and large posterior trunk after passing between tensor veli palatini, which is medial, and lateral pterygoid, which is lateral, and giving off a meningeal branch (nervus spinosus) and the nerve to medial pterygoid from its medial side.

nervous.name: Posterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: The posterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks innervate the extensor muscles.

nervous.name: Posterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: The posterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks innervate the extensor muscles.

nervous.name: Posterior fasciculus proprius
nervous.description: The proper fasciculi, or spinospinal fasciculi, or propriospinal tracts,[1] are groups of short fibres, ascending and descending, and crossed and uncrossed, within the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Posterior horn of spinal cord
nervous.description: The posterior grey column (posterior cornu, dorsal horn, spinal dorsal horn, posterior horn, sensory horn[1]) of the spinal cord is one of the three grey columns of the spinal cord.

nervous.name: Posterior interosseous nerve of forearm (left)
nervous.description: The posterior interosseous nerve (or dorsal interosseous nerve) is a nerve in the forearm.

nervous.name: Posterior interosseous nerve of forearm (right)
nervous.description: The posterior interosseous nerve (or dorsal interosseous nerve) is a nerve in the forearm.

nervous.name: Posterior nucleus of vagus nerve (left)
nervous.description: The dorsal nucleus of vagus nerve (or posterior nucleus of vagus nerve or dorsal vagal nucleus or nucleus dorsalis nervi vagi or nucleus posterior nervi vagi) is a cranial nerve nucleus for the vagus nerve in the medulla that lies ventral to the floor of the fourth ventricle.

nervous.name: Posterior nucleus of vagus nerve (right)
nervous.description: The dorsal nucleus of vagus nerve (or posterior nucleus of vagus nerve or dorsal vagal nucleus or nucleus dorsalis nervi vagi or nucleus posterior nervi vagi) is a cranial nerve nucleus for the vagus nerve in the medulla that lies ventral to the floor of the fourth ventricle.

nervous.name: Posterior root of spinal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The dorsal ramus of spinal nerve (or posterior ramus of spinal nerve, or posterior primary division) is the posterior division of a spinal nerve.

nervous.name: Posterior root of spinal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The dorsal ramus of spinal nerve (or posterior ramus of spinal nerve, or posterior primary division) is the posterior division of a spinal nerve.

nervous.name: Posterior segment of eyeball (left)
nervous.description: The posterior segment or posterior cavity is the back two-thirds of the eye that includes the anterior hyaloid membrane and all of the optical structures behind it: the vitreous humor, retina, choroid, and optic nerve.

nervous.name: Posterior segment of eyeball (right)
nervous.description: The posterior segment or posterior cavity is the back two-thirds of the eye that includes the anterior hyaloid membrane and all of the optical structures behind it: the vitreous humor, retina, choroid, and optic nerve.

nervous.name: Posterior spinocerebellar tract
nervous.description: The spinocerebellar tract is a nerve tract originating in the spinal cord and terminating in the same side (ipsilateral) of the cerebellum.

nervous.name: Posterolateral tract
nervous.description: The posterolateral tract (fasciculus of Lissauer, Lissauer's tract, tract of Lissauer, dorsolateral fasciculus, dorsolateral tract, zone of Lissauer) is a small strand situated in relation to the tip of the posterior column close to the entrance of the posterior nerve roots.

nervous.name: Precentral gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The precentral gyrus is a prominent gyrus on the surface of the posterior frontal lobe of the brain.

nervous.name: Precentral gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The precentral gyrus is a prominent gyrus on the surface of the posterior frontal lobe of the brain.

nervous.name: Precentral sulcus (inferior part)* (left)
nervous.description: The precentral sulcus is a part of the human brain that lies parallel to, and in front of, the central sulcus.

nervous.name: Precentral sulcus (inferior part)* (right)
nervous.description: The precentral sulcus is a part of the human brain that lies parallel to, and in front of, the central sulcus.

nervous.name: Precentral sulcus (Superior part)* (left)
nervous.description: The precentral sulcus is a part of the human brain that lies parallel to, and in front of, the central sulcus.

nervous.name: Precentral sulcus (Superior part)* (right)
nervous.description: The precentral sulcus is a part of the human brain that lies parallel to, and in front of, the central sulcus.

nervous.name: Precuneus (left)
nervous.description: The precuneus is the portion of the superior parietal lobule on the medial surface of each brain hemisphere.

nervous.name: Precuneus (right)
nervous.description: The precuneus is the portion of the superior parietal lobule on the medial surface of each brain hemisphere.

nervous.name: Proper palmar digital branches of median nerve (left)
nervous.description: In the palm of the hand the median nerve is covered by the skin and the palmar aponeurosis, and rests on the tendons of the flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Proper palmar digital branches of median nerve (right)
nervous.description: In the palm of the hand the median nerve is covered by the skin and the palmar aponeurosis, and rests on the tendons of the flexor muscles.

nervous.name: Proper palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The proper palmar digital nerves of the ulnar nerve are nerves of the hand.

nervous.name: Proper palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The proper palmar digital nerves of the ulnar nerve are nerves of the hand.

nervous.name: Proper plantar digital branches of lateral plantar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The proper plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve are nerves of the foot that arise from the superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve.

nervous.name: Proper plantar digital branches of lateral plantar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The proper plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve are nerves of the foot that arise from the superficial branch of the lateral plantar nerve.

nervous.name: Proper plantar digital branches of medial plantar nerve (left)
nervous.description: Plantar cutaneous nerves for the fibular and tibial sides of the 3,5 medial toes.

nervous.name: Proper plantar digital branches of medial plantar nerve (right)
nervous.description: Plantar cutaneous nerves for the fibular and tibial sides of the 3,5 medial toes.

nervous.name: Putamen (left)
nervous.description: The putamen (from Latin, meaning "nutshell") is a round structure located at the base of the forebrain (telencephalon).

nervous.name: Putamen (right)
nervous.description: The putamen (from Latin, meaning "nutshell") is a round structure located at the base of the forebrain (telencephalon).

nervous.name: Pyramid of medulla oblongata (left)
nervous.description: The medullary pyramids are paired white matter structures of the brainstem's medulla oblongata that contain motor fibers of the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts – known together as the pyramidal tracts.

nervous.name: Pyramid of medulla oblongata (right)
nervous.description: The medullary pyramids are paired white matter structures of the brainstem's medulla oblongata that contain motor fibers of the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts – known together as the pyramidal tracts.

nervous.name: Radial nerve (left)
nervous.description: The radial nerve is a nerve in the human body that supplies the posterior portion of the upper limb.

nervous.name: Radial nerve (right)
nervous.description: The radial nerve is a nerve in the human body that supplies the posterior portion of the upper limb.

nervous.name: Red nucleus (left)
nervous.description: The red nucleus or nucleus ruber is a structure in the rostral midbrain involved in motor coordination.

nervous.name: Red nucleus (right)
nervous.description: The red nucleus or nucleus ruber is a structure in the rostral midbrain involved in motor coordination.

nervous.name: Retina (left)
nervous.description: The retina (from Latin: rete "net") is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye of most vertebrates and some molluscs.

nervous.name: Retina (right)
nervous.description: The retina (from Latin: rete "net") is the innermost, light-sensitive layer of tissue of the eye of most vertebrates and some molluscs.

nervous.name: Roots of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: The five roots are the five anterior primary rami of the spinal nerves, after they have given off their segmental supply to the muscles of the neck.

nervous.name: Roots of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: The five roots are the five anterior primary rami of the spinal nerves, after they have given off their segmental supply to the muscles of the neck.

nervous.name: Rubrospinal tract
nervous.description: The rubrospinal tract is a part of the nervous system.

nervous.name: Saphenous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The saphenous nerve (long or internal saphenous nerve) is the largest cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve.

nervous.name: Saphenous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The saphenous nerve (long or internal saphenous nerve) is the largest cutaneous branch of the femoral nerve.

nervous.name: Sciatic nerve (left)
nervous.description: The sciatic nerve, also called the ischiadic nerve, is a large nerve in humans and other vertebrate animals which is the largest branch of the sacral plexus and runs alongside the hip joint and down the lower limb.

nervous.name: Sciatic nerve (right)
nervous.description: The sciatic nerve, also called the ischiadic nerve, is a large nerve in humans and other vertebrate animals which is the largest branch of the sacral plexus and runs alongside the hip joint and down the lower limb.

nervous.name: Sclera (left)
nervous.description: The sclera, also known as the white of the eye or, in older literature, as the tunica albuginea oculi, is the opaque, fibrous, protective, outer layer of the human eye containing mainly collagen and some crucial elastic fiber.

nervous.name: Sclera (right)
nervous.description: The sclera, also known as the white of the eye or, in older literature, as the tunica albuginea oculi, is the opaque, fibrous, protective, outer layer of the human eye containing mainly collagen and some crucial elastic fiber.

nervous.name: Sensory root of trigeminal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The principal sensory nucleus of trigeminal nerve (or chief sensory nucleus of V, main trigeminal sensory nucleus) is a group of second-order neurons which have cell bodies in the caudal pons.

nervous.name: Sensory root of trigeminal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The principal sensory nucleus of trigeminal nerve (or chief sensory nucleus of V, main trigeminal sensory nucleus) is a group of second-order neurons which have cell bodies in the caudal pons.

nervous.name: Septal nuclei
nervous.description: The septal area (medial olfactory area), consisting of the lateral septum and medial septum, is an area in the lower, posterior part of the medial surface of the frontal lobe, and refers to the nearby septum pellucidum.

nervous.name: Septum pellucidum
nervous.description: The septum pellucidum (Latin for "translucent wall") is a thin, triangular, vertical double membrane separating the anterior horns of the left and right lateral ventricles of the brain.

nervous.name: Spinal dura
nervous.description: Dura mater is a thick membrane made of dense irregular connective tissue that surrounds the brain and spinal cord.

nervous.name: Spinal ganglion (left)
nervous.description: A dorsal root ganglion (or spinal ganglion; also known as a posterior root ganglion) is a cluster of neurons (a ganglion) in a dorsal root of a spinal nerve.

nervous.name: Spinal ganglion (right)
nervous.description: A dorsal root ganglion (or spinal ganglion; also known as a posterior root ganglion) is a cluster of neurons (a ganglion) in a dorsal root of a spinal nerve.

nervous.name: Spinotectal tract
nervous.description: The spinotectal tract (spinomesencephalic tract, spinotectal fasciculus, spino-quadrigeminal system of Mott) arises in the spinothalamic tract and terminates in the inferior and superior colliculi.It is situated ventral to the lateral spinothalamic tract, but its fibers are more or less intermingled with it.

nervous.name: Straight gyrus (Gyrus rectus) (left)
nervous.description: The portion of the inferior frontal lobe immediately adjacent to the longitudinal fissure (and medial to the medial orbital gyrus and olfactory tract) is named the straight gyrus,(or gyrus rectus) and is continuous with the superior frontal gyrus on the medial surface.

nervous.name: Straight gyrus (Gyrus rectus) (right)
nervous.description: The portion of the inferior frontal lobe immediately adjacent to the longitudinal fissure (and medial to the medial orbital gyrus and olfactory tract) is named the straight gyrus,(or gyrus rectus) and is continuous with the superior frontal gyrus on the medial surface.

nervous.name: Stria medullaris thalami (left)
nervous.description: The stria medullaris is a part of the epithalamus.

nervous.name: Stria medullaris thalami (right)
nervous.description: The stria medullaris is a part of the epithalamus.

nervous.name: Stria terminalis (left)
nervous.description: The stria terminalis (or terminal stria) is a structure in the brain consisting of a band of fibers running along the lateral margin of the ventricular surface of the thalamus.

nervous.name: Stria terminalis (right)
nervous.description: The stria terminalis (or terminal stria) is a structure in the brain consisting of a band of fibers running along the lateral margin of the ventricular surface of the thalamus.

nervous.name: Subclavian nerve (left)
nervous.description: The subclavian nerve, also known as the nerve to the subclavius, is small branch of the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Subclavian nerve (right)
nervous.description: The subclavian nerve, also known as the nerve to the subclavius, is small branch of the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Subparietal sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The subparietal sulcus (Sulcus subparietalis) or suprasplenial sulcus is a sulcus, or crevice, on the medial surface of each cerebral hemisphere, above the splenium of the corpus callosum.

nervous.name: Subparietal sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The subparietal sulcus (Sulcus subparietalis) or suprasplenial sulcus is a sulcus, or crevice, on the medial surface of each cerebral hemisphere, above the splenium of the corpus callosum.

nervous.name: Superficial branch of radial nerve (left)
nervous.description: The superficial branch of the radial nerve passes along the front of the radial side of the forearm to the commencement of its lower third.

nervous.name: Superficial branch of radial nerve (right)
nervous.description: The superficial branch of the radial nerve passes along the front of the radial side of the forearm to the commencement of its lower third.

nervous.name: Superficial branch of ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: The superficial branch of the ulnar nerve is a terminal branch of the ulnar nerve.

nervous.name: Superficial branch of ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: The superficial branch of the ulnar nerve is a terminal branch of the ulnar nerve.

nervous.name: Superficial fibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The superficial fibular nerve, sometimes called the superficial peroneal nerve, innervates the peroneus longus and peroneus brevis muscles and the skin over the antero-lateral aspect of the leg along with the greater part of the dorsum of the foot (with the exception of the first web space, which is innervated by the deep fibular nerve).

nervous.name: Superficial fibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The superficial fibular nerve, sometimes called the superficial peroneal nerve, innervates the peroneus longus and peroneus brevis muscles and the skin over the antero-lateral aspect of the leg along with the greater part of the dorsum of the foot (with the exception of the first web space, which is innervated by the deep fibular nerve).

nervous.name: Superior cerebellar peduncle (left)
nervous.description: In the human brain, the superior cerebellar peduncle (brachium conjunctivum) is a paired structure of white matter that connects the cerebellum to the midbrain.

nervous.name: Superior cerebellar peduncle (right)
nervous.description: In the human brain, the superior cerebellar peduncle (brachium conjunctivum) is a paired structure of white matter that connects the cerebellum to the midbrain.

nervous.name: Superior colliculus (left)
nervous.description: The superior colliculus (Latin for upper hill) is a structure lying on the roof of the mammalian midbrain.

nervous.name: Superior colliculus (right)
nervous.description: The superior colliculus (Latin for upper hill) is a structure lying on the roof of the mammalian midbrain.

nervous.name: Superior frontal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The superior frontal gyrus (SFG) also marginal gyrus, makes up about one third of the frontal lobe of the human brain.

nervous.name: Superior frontal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The superior frontal gyrus (SFG) also marginal gyrus, makes up about one third of the frontal lobe of the human brain.

nervous.name: Superior frontal sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The superior frontal sulcus is a sulcus between the superior frontal gyrus and the middle frontal gyrus.

nervous.name: Superior frontal sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The superior frontal sulcus is a sulcus between the superior frontal gyrus and the middle frontal gyrus.

nervous.name: Superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve (left)
nervous.description: The superior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm (or superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve) is the continuation of the posterior cord of the axillary nerve, after it pierces the deep fascia.

nervous.name: Superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve (right)
nervous.description: The superior lateral cutaneous nerve of arm (or superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve) is the continuation of the posterior cord of the axillary nerve, after it pierces the deep fascia.

nervous.name: Superior occipital gyri (left)
nervous.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain.

nervous.name: Superior occipital gyri (right)
nervous.description: The occipital gyri (OcG) are three gyri in parallel, along the lateral portion of the occipital lobe, also referred to as a composite structure in the brain.

nervous.name: Superior parietal lobule (left)
nervous.description: The superior parietal lobule is bounded in front by the upper part of the postcentral sulcus, but is usually connected with the postcentral gyrus above the end of the sulcus.

nervous.name: Superior parietal lobule (right)
nervous.description: The superior parietal lobule is bounded in front by the upper part of the postcentral sulcus, but is usually connected with the postcentral gyrus above the end of the sulcus.

nervous.name: Superior salivatory nucleus (left)
nervous.description: The salivatory nuclei are the superior salivatory nucleus, and the inferior salivatory nucleus that innervate the salivary glands.

nervous.name: Superior salivatory nucleus (right)
nervous.description: The salivatory nuclei are the superior salivatory nucleus, and the inferior salivatory nucleus that innervate the salivary glands.

nervous.name: Superior temporal gyrus (Lateral part) (left)
nervous.description: The superior temporal gyrus (STG) is one of three (sometimes two) gyri in the temporal lobe of the human brain, which is located laterally to the head, situated somewhat above the external ear.

nervous.name: Superior temporal gyrus (Lateral part) (right)
nervous.description: The superior temporal gyrus (STG) is one of three (sometimes two) gyri in the temporal lobe of the human brain, which is located laterally to the head, situated somewhat above the external ear.

nervous.name: Superior temporal sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The superior temporal sulcus (STS) is the sulcus separating the superior temporal gyrus from the middle temporal gyrus in the temporal lobe of the brain.

nervous.name: Superior temporal sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The superior temporal sulcus (STS) is the sulcus separating the superior temporal gyrus from the middle temporal gyrus in the temporal lobe of the brain.

nervous.name: Superior trunk of brachial plexus (left)
nervous.description: The upper (superior) trunk is part of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Superior trunk of brachial plexus (right)
nervous.description: The upper (superior) trunk is part of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Supramarginal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: The supramarginal gyrus is a portion of the parietal lobe.

nervous.name: Supramarginal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: The supramarginal gyrus is a portion of the parietal lobe.

nervous.name: Suprascapular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The suprascapular nerve is a nerve that branches from the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Suprascapular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The suprascapular nerve is a nerve that branches from the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

nervous.name: Sural communicating branch of common fibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: Emerges in the popliteal fossa and is distributed laterally to the skin of the two thirds of the posterior surface of the leg.

nervous.name: Sural communicating branch of common fibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: Emerges in the popliteal fossa and is distributed laterally to the skin of the two thirds of the posterior surface of the leg.

nervous.name: Sural nerve (left)
nervous.description: The sural nerve is a sensory nerve in the calf region (sura) of the leg.

nervous.name: Sural nerve (right)
nervous.description: The sural nerve is a sensory nerve in the calf region (sura) of the leg.

nervous.name: Suspensory ligament of eyeball (left)
nervous.description: The suspensory ligament of eyeball (or Lockwood's ligament) forms a hammock stretching below the eyeball between the medial and lateral check ligaments and enclosing the inferior rectus and inferior oblique muscles of the eye.

nervous.name: Suspensory ligament of eyeball (right)
nervous.description: The suspensory ligament of eyeball (or Lockwood's ligament) forms a hammock stretching below the eyeball between the medial and lateral check ligaments and enclosing the inferior rectus and inferior oblique muscles of the eye.

nervous.name: Sympathetic nerves (left)
nervous.description: The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is one of two divisions of the autonomic nervous system, along with the parasympathetic nervous system.

nervous.name: Sympathetic nerves (right)
nervous.description: The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is one of two divisions of the autonomic nervous system, along with the parasympathetic nervous system.

nervous.name: Sympathetic trunk (left)
nervous.description: The sympathetic trunks (sympathetic chain, gangliated cord) are a paired bundle of nerve fibers that run from the base of the skull to the coccyx.

nervous.name: Sympathetic trunk (right)
nervous.description: The sympathetic trunks (sympathetic chain, gangliated cord) are a paired bundle of nerve fibers that run from the base of the skull to the coccyx.

nervous.name: Tectospinal tract
nervous.description: In humans, the tectospinal tract (or colliculospinal tract) is a nerve tract that coordinates head and eye movements.

nervous.name: Temporal plane (left)
nervous.description: The superior temporal gyrus (STG) is one of three (sometimes two) gyri in the temporal lobe of the human brain, which is located laterally to the head, situated somewhat above the external ear.

nervous.name: Temporal plane (right)
nervous.description: The superior temporal gyrus (STG) is one of three (sometimes two) gyri in the temporal lobe of the human brain, which is located laterally to the head, situated somewhat above the external ear.

nervous.name: Temporal pole (left)
nervous.description: There are three known poles of the cerebral hemispheres: the occipital pole, the frontal pole, and the temporal pole.

nervous.name: Temporal pole (right)
nervous.description: There are three known poles of the cerebral hemispheres: the occipital pole, the frontal pole, and the temporal pole.

nervous.name: Tentorium cerebelli (left)
nervous.description: The cerebellar tentorium or tentorium cerebelli (Latin for "tent of the cerebellum") is an extension of the dura mater that separates the cerebellum from the inferior portion of the occipital lobes.

nervous.name: Tentorium cerebelli (right)
nervous.description: The cerebellar tentorium or tentorium cerebelli (Latin for "tent of the cerebellum") is an extension of the dura mater that separates the cerebellum from the inferior portion of the occipital lobes.

nervous.name: Thalamus (left)
nervous.description: The thalamus (from Greek θάλαμος, "chamber") is a large mass of gray matter located in the dorsal part of the diencephalon (a division of the forebrain).

nervous.name: Thalamus (right)
nervous.description: The thalamus (from Greek θάλαμος, "chamber") is a large mass of gray matter located in the dorsal part of the diencephalon (a division of the forebrain).

nervous.name: Third ventricle
nervous.description: The third ventricle is one of the four connected ventricles of the ventricular system within the mammalian brain.

nervous.name: Thoracodorsal nerve (left)
nervous.description: The thoracodorsal nerve is a nerve present in humans and other animals, also known as the middle subscapular nerve or the long subscapular nerve.

nervous.name: Thoracodorsal nerve (right)
nervous.description: The thoracodorsal nerve is a nerve present in humans and other animals, also known as the middle subscapular nerve or the long subscapular nerve.

nervous.name: Tibial nerve (left)
nervous.description: The tibial nerve is a branch of the sciatic nerve.

nervous.name: Tibial nerve (right)
nervous.description: The tibial nerve is a branch of the sciatic nerve.

nervous.name: Transverse occipital sulcus (left)
nervous.description: The transverse occipital sulcus is a structure in the occipital lobe.

nervous.name: Transverse occipital sulcus (right)
nervous.description: The transverse occipital sulcus is a structure in the occipital lobe.

nervous.name: Transverse temporal gyri (left)
nervous.description: The transverse temporal gyri, also called Heschl's gyri  or Heschl's convolutions, are gyri found in the area of primary auditory cortex buried within the lateral sulcus of the human brain, occupying Brodmann areas 41 and 42.

nervous.name: Transverse temporal gyri (right)
nervous.description: The transverse temporal gyri, also called Heschl's gyri  or Heschl's convolutions, are gyri found in the area of primary auditory cortex buried within the lateral sulcus of the human brain, occupying Brodmann areas 41 and 42.

nervous.name: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus (left)
nervous.description: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus (pars triangularis), (cortex between the ascending ramus and the horizontal ramus of the lateral sulcus).

nervous.name: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus (right)
nervous.description: Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus (pars triangularis), (cortex between the ascending ramus and the horizontal ramus of the lateral sulcus).

nervous.name: Trigeminal nerve (V) (left)
nervous.description: The trigeminal nerve (the fifth cranial nerve, or simply CN V) is a nerve responsible for sensation in the face and motor functions such as biting and chewing; it is the most complex of the cranial nerves.

nervous.name: Trigeminal nerve (V) (right)
nervous.description: The trigeminal nerve (the fifth cranial nerve, or simply CN V) is a nerve responsible for sensation in the face and motor functions such as biting and chewing; it is the most complex of the cranial nerves.

nervous.name: Trochlear nerve (IV) (left)
nervous.description: The trochlear nerve, also called the fourth cranial nerve or CN IV, is a motor nerve (a somatic efferent nerve) that innervates just one muscle: the superior oblique muscle of the eye, which operates through the pulley-like trochlea.

nervous.name: Trochlear nerve (IV) (right)
nervous.description: The trochlear nerve, also called the fourth cranial nerve or CN IV, is a motor nerve (a somatic efferent nerve) that innervates just one muscle: the superior oblique muscle of the eye, which operates through the pulley-like trochlea.

nervous.name: Tuber of vermis
nervous.description: The tuber of vermis, the most posterior division of the inferior vermis, is of small size, and laterally spreads out into the large inferior semilunar lobules, which comprise at least two-thirds of the inferior surface of the hemisphere.

nervous.name: Tympanic membrane (left)
nervous.description: In the anatomy of humans and various other tetrapods, the eardrum, also called the tympanic membrane or myringa, is a thin, cone-shaped membrane that separates the external ear from the middle ear.

nervous.name: Tympanic membrane (right)
nervous.description: In the anatomy of humans and various other tetrapods, the eardrum, also called the tympanic membrane or myringa, is a thin, cone-shaped membrane that separates the external ear from the middle ear.

nervous.name: Ulnar nerve (left)
nervous.description: In human anatomy, the ulnar nerve is a nerve that runs near the ulna bone.

nervous.name: Ulnar nerve (right)
nervous.description: In human anatomy, the ulnar nerve is a nerve that runs near the ulna bone.

nervous.name: Vagus nerve (X) (left)
nervous.description: The vagus nerve, historically cited as the pneumogastric nerve, is the tenth cranial nerve or CN X, and interfaces with the parasympathetic control of the heart, lungs, and digestive tract.

nervous.name: Vagus nerve (X) (right)
nervous.description: The vagus nerve, historically cited as the pneumogastric nerve, is the tenth cranial nerve or CN X, and interfaces with the parasympathetic control of the heart, lungs, and digestive tract.

nervous.name: Vestibular nerve (left)
nervous.description: The vestibular nerve is one of the two branches of the vestibulocochlear nerve (the cochlear nerve being the other).

nervous.name: Vestibular nerve (right)
nervous.description: The vestibular nerve is one of the two branches of the vestibulocochlear nerve (the cochlear nerve being the other).

nervous.name: Vestibular nuclei (left)
nervous.description: The vestibular nuclei (VN) are the cranial nuclei for the vestibular nerve located in the brainstem. In Terminologia Anatomica they are grouped in both the pons and the medulla in the brainstem.

nervous.name: Vestibular nuclei (right)
nervous.description: The vestibular nuclei (VN) are the cranial nuclei for the vestibular nerve located in the brainstem. In Terminologia Anatomica they are grouped in both the pons and the medulla in the brainstem.

nervous.name: Vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII) (left)
nervous.description: The vestibulocochlear nerve (auditory vestibular nerve), known as the eighth cranial nerve, transmits sound and equilibrium (balance) information from the inner ear to the brain.

nervous.name: Vestibulocochlear nerve (VIII) (right)
nervous.description: The vestibulocochlear nerve (auditory vestibular nerve), known as the eighth cranial nerve, transmits sound and equilibrium (balance) information from the inner ear to the brain.

nervous.name: Vitreous body (left)
nervous.description: The vitreous body (vitreous meaning "glass-like", from Latin vitreus, equivalent to vitr(um) glass + -eus -ous) is the clear gel that fills the space between the lens and the retina of the eyeball (the vitreous chamber) in humans and other vertebrates.

nervous.name: Vitreous body (right)
nervous.description: The vitreous body (vitreous meaning "glass-like", from Latin vitreus, equivalent to vitr(um) glass + -eus -ous) is the clear gel that fills the space between the lens and the retina of the eyeball (the vitreous chamber) in humans and other vertebrates.

nervous.name: White matter of spinal cord
nervous.description: In cross-section, the peripheral region of the cord contains neuronal white matter tracts containing sensory and motor axons.

nervous.name: White matter of telencephalon (left)
nervous.description: White matter refers to areas of the central nervous system (CNS) that are mainly made up of myelinated axons, also called tracts.

nervous.name: White matter of telencephalon (right)
nervous.description: White matter refers to areas of the central nervous system (CNS) that are mainly made up of myelinated axons, also called tracts.

reproductive.name: Corpus cavernosum of penis
reproductive.description: A corpus cavernosum penis (singular) (literally "cave-like body" of the penis, plural corpora cavernosa) is one of a pair of sponge-like regions of erectile tissue, which contain most of the blood in the penis during an erection.

reproductive.name: Corpus spongiosum of penis
reproductive.description: The corpus spongiosum is the mass of spongy tissue surrounding the male urethra within the penis.

reproductive.name: Ductus deferens (left)
reproductive.description: The vas deferens, or ductus deferens, is part of the male reproductive system of many vertebrates.

reproductive.name: Ductus deferens (right)
reproductive.description: The vas deferens, or ductus deferens, is part of the male reproductive system of many vertebrates.

reproductive.name: Ejaculatory duct (left)
reproductive.description: The ejaculatory ducts (ductus ejaculatorii) are paired structures in male anatomy.

reproductive.name: Ejaculatory duct (right)
reproductive.description: The ejaculatory ducts (ductus ejaculatorii) are paired structures in male anatomy.

reproductive.name: Epididymis (left)
reproductive.description: The epididymis (plural: epididymides or) is a tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens in the male reproductive system.

reproductive.name: Epididymis (right)
reproductive.description: The epididymis (plural: epididymides or) is a tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens in the male reproductive system.

reproductive.name: Glans penis
reproductive.description: The glans penis, commonly referred to as the glans, is a structure at the distal end of the penis in male mammals.

reproductive.name: Prostate
reproductive.description: The prostate is both an accessory gland of the male reproductive system and a muscle-driven mechanical switch between urination and ejaculation.

reproductive.name: Seminal gland (left)
reproductive.description: The seminal vesicles (also called vesicular glands, or seminal glands) are a pair of two convoluted tubular glands that lie behind the urinary bladder of some male mammals.

reproductive.name: Seminal gland (right)
reproductive.description: The seminal vesicles (also called vesicular glands, or seminal glands) are a pair of two convoluted tubular glands that lie behind the urinary bladder of some male mammals.

reproductive.name: Testis (left)
reproductive.description: Testicle or testis (plural testes) is the male reproductive gland or gonad in all animals, including humans.

reproductive.name: Testis (right)
reproductive.description: Testicle or testis (plural testes) is the male reproductive gland or gonad in all animals, including humans.

reproductive-female.name: Broad ligament of uterus (left)
reproductive-female.description: The broad ligament of the uterus is the wide fold of peritoneum that connects the sides of the uterus to the walls and floor of the pelvis.

reproductive-female.name: Broad ligament of uterus (right)
reproductive-female.description: The broad ligament of the uterus is the wide fold of peritoneum that connects the sides of the uterus to the walls and floor of the pelvis.

reproductive-female.name: Bulb of vestibule
reproductive-female.description: In female anatomy, the vestibular bulbs, bulbs of the vestibule or clitoral bulbs are two elongated masses of erectile tissue typically described as being situated on either side of the vaginal opening.

reproductive-female.name: Clitoris
reproductive-female.description: The clitoris is a female sex organ present in mammals, ostriches and a limited number of other animals.

reproductive-female.name: Labia minora
reproductive-female.description: The labia minora (Latin for smaller lips, singular: labium minus "smaller lip"), also known as the inner labia, inner lips, vaginal lips or nymphae, are two flaps of skin on either side of the human vaginal opening in the vulva, situated between the labia majora (Latin for larger lips; also called outer labia, or outer lips).

reproductive-female.name: Ovary (left)
reproductive-female.description: The ovary is an organ found in the female reproductive system that produces an ovum.

reproductive-female.name: Ovary (right)
reproductive-female.description: The ovary is an organ found in the female reproductive system that produces an ovum.

reproductive-female.name: Round ligament of uterus (left)
reproductive-female.description: The round ligament of the uterus is a ligament that connects the uterus to the labia majora.

reproductive-female.name: Round ligament of uterus (right)
reproductive-female.description: The round ligament of the uterus is a ligament that connects the uterus to the labia majora.

reproductive-female.name: Uterine tube (left)
reproductive-female.description: The Fallopian tubes, also known as uterine tubes, salpinges (singular salpinx), or oviducts, are tubes that stretch from the ovaries to the uterus, in the human female reproductive system.

reproductive-female.name: Uterine tube (right)
reproductive-female.description: The Fallopian tubes, also known as uterine tubes, salpinges (singular salpinx), or oviducts, are tubes that stretch from the ovaries to the uterus, in the human female reproductive system.

reproductive-female.name: Uterus
reproductive-female.description: The uterus (from Latin "uterus", plural uteri) or womb is the main female hormone-responsive, secondary sex organ of the reproductive system in humans and most other mammals.

reproductive-female.name: Vagina
reproductive-female.description: In mammals, the vagina is the elastic, muscular part of the female genital tract.

respiratory.name: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BVIII)
respiratory.description: For the basal segment that touches the inferior part of the anterior border of the lung.

respiratory.name: Anterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BVIII)
respiratory.description: For the anterior segment, corner-shaped, of the inferior lobe.

respiratory.name: Anterior segmental bronchus of left lung (BIII)
respiratory.description: For the anterior segment taht extends rearwards to approximately the midaxillary line.

respiratory.name: Anterior segmental bronchus of right lung (BIII)
respiratory.description: For the anterior segment, that extends rearwards until approximately the midaxillary line.

respiratory.name: Apical segmental bronchus of right lung (BI)
respiratory.description: For the apical segment of right lung, that extends until the third rib bellow.

respiratory.name: Apicoposterior segmental bronchus of left lung (BI+BII)
respiratory.description: For the segment located in the superior and posterior part of the superior lobe of left lung.

respiratory.name: Epiglottis
respiratory.description: The epiglottis is a leaf-shaped flap in the throat that prevents food from entering the windpipe and the lungs.

respiratory.name: Inferior lingular segmental bronchus of left lung (BV)
respiratory.description: For the lower segment of the superior lobe of left lung, mainly anterior.

respiratory.name: Inferior lobe of left lung
respiratory.description: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

respiratory.name: Inferior lobe of right lung
respiratory.description: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

respiratory.name: Intermediate bronchus (right)
respiratory.description: The bronchus intermedius runs distal to the right upper lobe bifurcation and follows the trajectory of the right main bronchus.

respiratory.name: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BIX)
respiratory.description: For the basal segment, in intermediary situation between the anterior and posterior basal segments.

respiratory.name: Lateral basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BIX)
respiratory.description: For the small lateral segment, located between the anterior and the posterior segments.

respiratory.name: Lateral segmental bronchus of right lung (BIV)
respiratory.description: For the lateral segment, located dorsally to the middle lobe.

respiratory.name: Left inferior lobar bronchus
respiratory.description: For the inferior lobe that extends upwards until the fourth thoracic vertebra.

respiratory.name: Left main bronchus
respiratory.description: A bronchus is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.

respiratory.name: Left superior lobar bronchus
respiratory.description: For the left superior lobe.

respiratory.name: Medial basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BVII)
respiratory.description: For the medial basal segment that does not reach the external surface of the lung.

respiratory.name: Medial basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BVII)
respiratory.description: For the medial segment of the inferior lobe, that does not reach the external surface of this lobe.

respiratory.name: Medial segmental bronchus of right lung (BV)
respiratory.description: For the medial segment, located medially in the middle lobe.

respiratory.name: Middle lobar bronchus (right)
respiratory.description: For the middle lobe of right lung.

respiratory.name: Middle lobe of right lung
respiratory.description: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

respiratory.name: Pleura
respiratory.description: The pulmonary pleurae (sing. pleura) are the two opposing layers of serous membrane overlying the lungs and the inside of the surrounding chest walls.

respiratory.name: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of left lung (BX)
respiratory.description: For the segment located beneath the superior segment of the inferior lobe.

respiratory.name: Posterior basal segmental bronchus of right lung (BX)
respiratory.description: For the posterior segment that extends rearwards until the vertebral column.

respiratory.name: Posterior segmental bronchus of right lung (BII)
respiratory.description: For the posterior segment, that extends approximately until the midaxillary line.

respiratory.name: Right inferior lobar bronchus
respiratory.description: For the right inferior lobe, going back up rearward until the fourth rib.

respiratory.name: Right main bronchus
respiratory.description: A bronchus is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.

respiratory.name: Right superior lobar bronchus
respiratory.description: The eparterial bronchus (right superior lobar bronchus) is a branch of the right main bronchus given off about 2.5 cm from the bifurcation of the trachea.

respiratory.name: Superior lingular segmental bronchus of left lung (BIV)
respiratory.description: For the second lower segment of the left superior lobe, reaching rearward the limit of the inferior lobe.

respiratory.name: Superior lobe of left lung
respiratory.description: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

respiratory.name: Superior lobe of right lung
respiratory.description: The lungs are the primary organs of the respiratory system in humans and most other animals including a few fish, and some snails.

respiratory.name: Superior segmental bronchus of left lung (BVI)
respiratory.description: For the apical segment, in postero-superior situation in the inferior lobe.

respiratory.name: Superior segmental bronchus of right lung (BVI)
respiratory.description: For the apical segment, in contact only with the superior lobe.

respiratory.name: Trachea
respiratory.description: The trachea, also known as the windpipe, is a cartilaginous tube that connects the larynx to the bronchi of the lungs, allowing the passage of air, and so is present in almost all air-breathing animals with lungs.

skeletal.name: Acetabular labrum (left)
skeletal.description: The acetabular labrum (glenoidal labrum of the hip joint or cotyloid ligament in older texts) is a ring of cartilage that surrounds the acetabulum of the hip.

skeletal.name: Acetabular labrum (right)
skeletal.description: The acetabular labrum (glenoidal labrum of the hip joint or cotyloid ligament in older texts) is a ring of cartilage that surrounds the acetabulum of the hip.

skeletal.name: Acromioclavicular ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The acromioclavicular ligament is part of the acromioclavicular joint.

skeletal.name: Annular ligament of radius (left)
skeletal.description: The annular ligament (orbicular ligament) is a strong band of fibers that encircles the head of the radius, and retains it in contact with the radial notch of the ulna.

skeletal.name: Annular ligament of radius (right)
skeletal.description: The annular ligament (orbicular ligament) is a strong band of fibers that encircles the head of the radius, and retains it in contact with the radial notch of the ulna.

skeletal.name: Anterior cruciate ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) is one of a pair of cruciate ligaments (the other being the posterior cruciate ligament) in the human knee.

skeletal.name: Anterior cruciate ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) is one of a pair of cruciate ligaments (the other being the posterior cruciate ligament) in the human knee.

skeletal.name: Anterior ligament of fibular head (left)
skeletal.description: The anterior ligament of the head of the fibula (anterior superior ligament) consists of two or three broad and flat bands, which pass obliquely upward from the front of the head of the fibula to the front of the lateral condyle of the tibia.

skeletal.name: Anterior ligament of fibular head (right)
skeletal.description: The anterior ligament of the head of the fibula (anterior superior ligament) consists of two or three broad and flat bands, which pass obliquely upward from the front of the head of the fibula to the front of the lateral condyle of the tibia.

skeletal.name: Anterior longitudinal ligament
skeletal.description: The anterior longitudinal ligament is a ligament that runs down the anterior surface of the spine.

skeletal.name: Anterior sacro-iliac ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The anterior sacroiliac ligament consists of numerous thin bands, which connect the anterior surface of the lateral part of the sacrum to the margin of the auricular surface of the ilium and to the preauricular sulcus.

skeletal.name: Anterior sacro-iliac ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The anterior sacroiliac ligament consists of numerous thin bands, which connect the anterior surface of the lateral part of the sacrum to the margin of the auricular surface of the ilium and to the preauricular sulcus.

skeletal.name: Anterior sternoclavicular ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The anterior sternoclavicular ligament is a broad band of fibers, covering the anterior (front) surface of the joint between the sternum and clavicle (sternoclavicular articulation).

skeletal.name: Anterior sternoclavicular ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The anterior sternoclavicular ligament is a broad band of fibers, covering the anterior (front) surface of the joint between the sternum and clavicle (sternoclavicular articulation).

skeletal.name: Anterior talocalcaneal ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The anterior talocalcaneal ligament (anterior calcaneo-astragaloid ligament or anterior interosseous ligament) is a ligament in the foot. The anterior talocalcaneal ligament extends from the front and lateral surface of the neck of the talus to the sinus tarsi of the calcaneus.

skeletal.name: Anterior talocalcaneal ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The anterior talocalcaneal ligament (anterior calcaneo-astragaloid ligament or anterior interosseous ligament) is a ligament in the foot. The anterior talocalcaneal ligament extends from the front and lateral surface of the neck of the talus to the sinus tarsi of the calcaneus.

skeletal.name: Anterior talofibular ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The anterior talofibular ligament is a ligament in the ankle. It passes from the anterior margin of the fibular malleolus, anteriorly and laterally, to the talus bone, in front of its lateral articular facet.

skeletal.name: Anterior talofibular ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The anterior talofibular ligament is a ligament in the ankle. It passes from the anterior margin of the fibular malleolus, anteriorly and laterally, to the talus bone, in front of its lateral articular facet.

skeletal.name: Anterior tibiofibular ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The anterior ligament of the lateral malleolus (anterior tibiofibular ligament or anterior inferior ligament) is a flat, trapezoidal band of fibers, broader below than above, which extends obliquely downward and lateralward between the adjacent margins of the tibia and fibula, on the front aspect of the syndesmosis.

skeletal.name: Anterior tibiofibular ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The anterior ligament of the lateral malleolus (anterior tibiofibular ligament or anterior inferior ligament) is a flat, trapezoidal band of fibers, broader below than above, which extends obliquely downward and lateralward between the adjacent margins of the tibia and fibula, on the front aspect of the syndesmosis.

skeletal.name: Arcuate popliteal ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The arcuate popliteal ligament is an extracapsular ligament of the knee.

skeletal.name: Arcuate popliteal ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The arcuate popliteal ligament is an extracapsular ligament of the knee.

skeletal.name: Articular capsule of glenohumeral joint (left)

skeletal.name: Articular capsule of glenohumeral joint (right)
skeletal.description: The human shoulder is made up of three bones: the clavicle (collarbone), the scapula (shoulder blade), and the humerus (upper arm bone) as well as associated muscles, ligaments and tendons.

skeletal.name: Articular capsule of hip joint (right)

skeletal.description: In humans and other primates, the knee joins the thigh with the leg and consists of two joints: one between the femur and tibia (tibiofemoral joint), and one between the femur and patella (patellofemoral joint).

skeletal.name: Articular capsule of knee joint (right)
skeletal.description: In humans and other primates, the knee joins the thigh with the leg and consists of two joints: one between the femur and tibia (tibiofemoral joint), and one between the femur and patella (patellofemoral joint).

skeletal.name: Articular disc of distal radio-ulnar joint (left)
skeletal.description: The radiocarpal joint or wrist joint is an ellipsoid joint formed by the radius and the triangular articular disc proximally and the proximal row of carpal bones distally.

skeletal.name: Articular disc of distal radio-ulnar joint (right)
skeletal.description: The radiocarpal joint or wrist joint is an ellipsoid joint formed by the radius and the triangular articular disc proximally and the proximal row of carpal bones distally.

skeletal.name: Articular disc of sternoclavicular joint (left)
skeletal.description: The articular disc of the sternoclavicular joint is flat and nearly circular, interposed between the articulating surfaces of the sternum and clavicle.

skeletal.name: Articular disc of sternoclavicular joint (right)
