skeletal.name: Articular disc of temporomandibular joint (left)
skeletal.description: The articular disk of the temporomandibular joint is a thin, oval plate made of non-vascular fibrous connective tissue, which is located between the mandible's condyloid process and the cranium's mandibular fossa.

skeletal.name: Articular disc of temporomandibular joint (right)
skeletal.description: The articular disk of the temporomandibular joint is a thin, oval plate made of non-vascular fibrous connective tissue, which is located between the mandible's condyloid process and the cranium's mandibular fossa.

skeletal.name: Arytenoid cartilage (left)
skeletal.description: The arytenoid cartilages  are a pair of small three-sided pyramids which form part of the larynx.

skeletal.name: Arytenoid cartilage (right)
skeletal.description: The arytenoid cartilages  are a pair of small three-sided pyramids which form part of the larynx.

skeletal.name: Atlas (C1)
skeletal.description: In anatomy, the atlas (C1) is the most superior (first) cervical vertebra of the spine and is located in the neck.

skeletal.name: Axis (C2)
skeletal.description: In anatomy, the axis (from Latin axis, "axle") or epistropheus, is the second cervical vertebra (C2) of the spine, immediately posterior to the atlas, upon which the head rests.

skeletal.name: Body of sternum
skeletal.description: The body, or gladiolus, is the longest sternal part.

skeletal.name: Calcaneocuboid ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The Calcaneocuboid ligament is a fibrous band that connects the superior surface of the calcaneus to the dorsal surface of the cuboid bone. It forms part of the bifurcated ligament.

skeletal.name: Calcaneocuboid ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The Calcaneocuboid ligament is a fibrous band that connects the superior surface of the calcaneus to the dorsal surface of the cuboid bone. It forms part of the bifurcated ligament.

skeletal.name: Calcaneofibular ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The calcaneofibular ligament is a narrow, rounded cord, running from the tip of the lateral malleolus of the fibula downward and slightly backward to a tubercle on the lateral surface of the calcaneus.

skeletal.name: Calcaneofibular ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The calcaneofibular ligament is a narrow, rounded cord, running from the tip of the lateral malleolus of the fibula downward and slightly backward to a tubercle on the lateral surface of the calcaneus.

skeletal.name: Calcaneonavicular ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The calcaneonavicular ligament is the upper of two parts of the bifurcate ligament that is divided in front in a Y-shaped manner into a calcaneocuboid ligament and a calcaneonavicular part.

skeletal.name: Calcaneonavicular ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The calcaneonavicular ligament is the upper of two parts of the bifurcate ligament that is divided in front in a Y-shaped manner into a calcaneocuboid ligament and a calcaneonavicular part.

skeletal.name: Calcaneus (left)
skeletal.description: In humans and many other primates, the calcaneus (from the Latin calcaneus or calcaneum, meaning heel) or heel bone is a bone of the tarsus of the foot which constitutes the heel.

skeletal.name: Calcaneus (right)
skeletal.description: In humans and many other primates, the calcaneus (from the Latin calcaneus or calcaneum, meaning heel) or heel bone is a bone of the tarsus of the foot which constitutes the heel.

skeletal.name: Capitate bone (left)
skeletal.description: The capitate bone is found in the center of the carpal bone region, colloquially known as the wrist, which is at the distal end of the radius and ulna bones.

skeletal.name: Capitate bone (right)
skeletal.description: The capitate bone is found in the center of the carpal bone region, colloquially known as the wrist, which is at the distal end of the radius and ulna bones.

skeletal.name: Clavicle (left)
skeletal.description: The clavicle, or collarbone, is a slender, S-shaped long bone approximately 6 inches (15 cm) long that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum (breastbone).

skeletal.name: Clavicle (right)
skeletal.description: The clavicle, or collarbone, is a slender, S-shaped long bone approximately 6 inches (15 cm) long that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum (breastbone).

skeletal.name: Coccyx
skeletal.description: The coccyx (plural: coccyges or coccyxes), commonly referred to as the tailbone, is the final segment of the vertebral column in all apes, and analogous structures in certain other mammals such as horses.

skeletal.name: Collateral interphalangeal ligaments of foot (left)
skeletal.description: The collateral ligaments of the interphalangeal joints of the foot are fibrous bands that are situated on both sides of the interphalangeal joints of the toes.

skeletal.name: Collateral interphalangeal ligaments of foot (right)
skeletal.description: The collateral ligaments of the interphalangeal joints of the foot are fibrous bands that are situated on both sides of the interphalangeal joints of the toes.

skeletal.name: Collateral interphalangeal ligaments of hand (left)
skeletal.description: On each side of the interphalangeal joints of the fingers are diagonally placed fibrous bands.

skeletal.name: Collateral interphalangeal ligaments of hand (right)
skeletal.description: On each side of the interphalangeal joints of the fingers are diagonally placed fibrous bands.

skeletal.name: Collateral metacarpophalangeal ligaments (left)
skeletal.description: In human anatomy, the radial (RCL) and ulnar (UCL) collateral ligaments of the metacarpophalangeal joints (MCP) of the hand are the primary stabilisers of the MCP joints.

skeletal.name: Collateral metacarpophalangeal ligaments (right)
skeletal.description: In human anatomy, the radial (RCL) and ulnar (UCL) collateral ligaments of the metacarpophalangeal joints (MCP) of the hand are the primary stabilisers of the MCP joints.

skeletal.name: Collateral metatarsophalangeal ligaments (left)
skeletal.description: The collateral ligaments of metatarsophalangeal joints are strong, rounded cords, placed one on either side of each joint, and attached, by one end, to the posterior tubercle on the side of the head of the metatarsal bone, and, by the other, to the contiguous extremity of the phalanx.

skeletal.name: Collateral metatarsophalangeal ligaments (right)
skeletal.description: The collateral ligaments of metatarsophalangeal joints are strong, rounded cords, placed one on either side of each joint, and attached, by one end, to the posterior tubercle on the side of the head of the metatarsal bone, and, by the other, to the contiguous extremity of the phalanx.

skeletal.name: Conoid ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The conoid ligament is the posterior and medial fasciculus of the coracoclavicular ligament.

skeletal.name: Conoid ligament (right)

skeletal.name: Coraco-acromial ligament (left)

skeletal.name: Coraco-acromial ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The coracoacromial ligament is a strong triangular ligament between the coracoid process and the acromion.

skeletal.name: Coracohumeral ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The coracohumeral ligament is a broad ligament which strengthens the upper part of the capsule of the shoulder joint.

skeletal.name: Coracohumeral ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The coracohumeral ligament is a broad ligament which strengthens the upper part of the capsule of the shoulder joint.

skeletal.name: Corniculate cartilage (left)
skeletal.description: The corniculate cartilages are two small conical nodules consisting of elastic cartilage, which articulate with the summits of the arytenoid cartilages and serve to prolong them posteriorly and medially.

skeletal.name: Corniculate cartilage (right)
skeletal.description: The corniculate cartilages are two small conical nodules consisting of elastic cartilage, which articulate with the summits of the arytenoid cartilages and serve to prolong them posteriorly and medially.

skeletal.name: Costoclavicular ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The costoclavicular ligament also known as the rhomboid ligament or Halsted's ligament is a ligament of the shoulder girdle.

skeletal.name: Costoclavicular ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The costoclavicular ligament also known as the rhomboid ligament or Halsted's ligament is a ligament of the shoulder girdle.

skeletal.name: Costotransverse ligament (left)

skeletal.name: Costotransverse ligament (right)
skeletal.description: A costotransverse ligament is a short fibrous band that connects a rib with the transverse process of vertebra.

skeletal.name: Cricoid cartilage
skeletal.description: The cricoid cartilage, or simply cricoid (from the Greek krikoeides meaning "ring-shaped") or cricoid ring, is the only complete ring of cartilage around the trachea.

skeletal.name: Cricopharyngeal ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The Cricopharyngeal ligament extends from the cricoid lamina to the midline of the pharynx.

skeletal.name: Cricopharyngeal ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The Cricopharyngeal ligament extends from the cricoid lamina to the midline of the pharynx.

skeletal.name: Cuboid bone (left)

skeletal.name: Cuboid bone (right)

skeletal.name: Deep part of tibial collateral ligament (left)

skeletal.name: Deep part of tibial collateral ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The tibial collateral ligament (TCL), or Medial collateral ligament (MCL) is one of the four major ligaments of the knee.

skeletal.name: Deep transverse metacarpal ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The deep transverse metacarpal ligament (also called the deep transverse palmar ligament) is a narrow fibrous band which runs across the palmar surfaces of the heads of the second, third, fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, connecting them together.

skeletal.name: Deep transverse metacarpal ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The deep transverse metacarpal ligament (also called the deep transverse palmar ligament) is a narrow fibrous band which runs across the palmar surfaces of the heads of the second, third, fourth and fifth metacarpal bones, connecting them together.

skeletal.name: Deep transverse metatarsal ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The transverse metatarsal ligament is a narrow band which runs across and connects together the heads of all the metatarsal bones.

skeletal.name: Deep transverse metatarsal ligament (right)
skeletal.description: The transverse metatarsal ligament is a narrow band which runs across and connects together the heads of all the metatarsal bones.

skeletal.name: Distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot (left)
skeletal.description: The phalanx (Ancient Greek: φάλαγξ; plural phalanxes or phalanges, φάλαγγες, phalanges) was a rectangular mass military formation, usually composed entirely of heavy infantry armed with spears, pikes, sarissas, or similar pole weapons.

skeletal.name: Distal phalanx of fifth finger of foot (right)
skeletal.description: The phalanx (Ancient Greek: φάλαγξ; plural phalanxes or phalanges, φάλαγγες, phalanges) was a rectangular mass military formation, usually composed entirely of heavy infantry armed with spears, pikes, sarissas, or similar pole weapons.

skeletal.name: Distal phalanx of fifth finger of hand (left)

skeletal.description: The pubic symphysis is a secondary cartilaginous joint between the left and right superior rami of the pubis of the hip bones.

skeletal.description: The pubofemoral ligament (pubocapsular ligament) is a ligament on the inferior side of the hip joint. This ligament is attached, above, to the obturator crest and the superior ramus of the pubis; below, it blends with the capsule and with the deep surface of the vertical band of the iliofemoral ligament.

skeletal.name: Radial collateral ligament (left)
skeletal.description: The radial collateral ligament (RCL), lateral collateral ligament (LCL), or external lateral ligament is a ligament in the elbow on the side of the radius.

skeletal.name: Radial collateral ligament of wrist joint (left)
skeletal.description: The radial collateral ligament (external lateral ligament, radial carpal collateral ligament) extends from the tip of the styloid process of the radius and attaches to the radial side of the scaphoid (formerly Navicular bone of the hand), immediately adjacent to its proximal articular surface and some fibres extend to the lateral side of the trapezium (greater multangular bone).

skeletal.name: Radial collateral ligament of wrist joint (right)

skeletal.name: Radiate ligament of head of rib (right)

skeletal.name: Sacrum
skeletal.description: The sacrum (plural: sacra or sacrums), in human anatomy, is a large, triangular bone at the base of the spine that forms by the fusing of the sacral vertebrae (S1–S5) between ages 18 and 30.The sacrum situates at the upper, back part of the pelvic cavity, between the two wings of the pelvis.

urinary.name: Urinary bladder
